# Motion Atlas packet 01 implementation report

**🟡 Implementation and fix rounds 1 and 2 committed. Fresh scoped review and integration remain.**

Five complete content contracts and distinct renderers are ready for coordinator review. DecisionFork reuses its accepted renderer and word-aware layout. No central registry, generated catalog, product source, database, deployment or external publication changed.

## Source and review boundary

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Worktree | `/Users/juanpablosarmiento/src/worktrees/avandar/feat/motion-catalog` |
| Branch | `feat/motion-catalog` |
| Base | `e9deb3d18` |

| Mutation ownership | One packet worker. No subagents or worker animation browser/raster rendering. |
| Source scope | Five owned preset directories, approved FitText module/test, approved shared-scene-library FitText API row. |

## Complete contracts and semantic behavior

Each directory exports its named renderer and `Props`, inferred `Input` and `inputSchema`, `defaultInput`, `fixtures`, `metadata`, and a descriptive camelCase contract satisfying `StockContract<Input>`. The contracts contain full strict structural JSON Schema, semantic rules, recursive serializable controls, indexed default text paths, a complete fictional binding, schema/metadata versions, collection and all fixtures. Content modules never import renderer/TSX modules. All four new defaults and metadata wording come from the accepted catalog. The existing DecisionFork metadata/defaults remain authoritative and retain every established public export. Public descriptors omit private provenance.

| Preset and contract export | Schema relations | Observed semantic behavior |
|---|---|---|
| PairedContrast / `pairedContrastContract` | Exactly two unique alternatives. One to three unique criteria. Focus references a criterion. Strict nested keys. | Equal labeled halves separate around the question. Matching pairs share baselines and bracket timing. One nominated row expands its comparison band. Switching focus keeps both alternatives and every criterion. Brackets toggle independently. |
| CapabilityMatrix / `capabilityMatrixContract` | Two to three unique options. Two to five unique rows. Exactly one cell per option in every row. Conditional cells require a nonblank qualification. Focus references its row/column, or uses an empty ID for none. | A skeleton settles before row-wise resolution. Check, horizontal absence line, conditional triangle and question-mark path are distinct. Focus changes only the bracket. Local querying, remote invitations and optional synchronization keep independent supplied states. Notes toggle without changing values. |
| RejectAndReplace / `rejectAndReplaceContract` | Strict complete criterion, option/rationale objects, state labels, link toggle and cross/strike enum. | Original starts in slot center x=480, moves to x=156, and retains its reason and rejection marker. Replacement occupies x=480 and receives its selection bracket and reason. Cross and strike use different path geometry without crossing rationale text. |
| DecisionFork / `decisionForkContract` | Existing unique branches and selected-reference validator reused. Two to four branches. | Existing single marker, selected outcome emphasis, closed unused gates and hidden-unchosen-outcome behavior verified. Renderer geometry, timing and accepted ForkLabel behavior remain in place. The renderer file only adds a documented exported Props type. |
| TradeoffPivot / `tradeoffPivotContract` | One to three unique points on each side. IDs are scoped to a side. Strict labels, authored priority and reveal-order enum. | Both equal leaves unfold and remain readable. Reversing order swaps their entrance sequence. Fixed editorial hinge angles and settled geometry do not depend on list counts and never become scores. Priority locks after both leaves open. |

All contracts use six-second, 180-frame content and the current 960 x 600 SVG convention. The outer StockGraphic continues to own the existing opaque seam envelope, delivery dimensions and frame gate. New entries are not registered by this worker, so direct SVG component SSR tests exercise their implementations without central edits.

## Layout and text limits

The accepted catalog character and collection limits remain unchanged. No font shrinking, truncation, clipping or dropped visible text is introduced. Every preset has complete default, minimum, dense and changed fixtures. Dense fixtures use maximum-length unbroken wide Unicode text, not shorter convenient labels.

| Preset | Fixed text and slots | Vertical limits |
|---|---|---|
| PairedContrast | Question 24px / 840px / 3 lines. Alternatives 20px / 312px / 2 lines. Criterion 14px / 144px / 3 lines. Attribute sides 18px / 288px / 3 lines. Caption 16px / 840px / 2 lines. | Up to three rows on 94px spacing. Caption starts y=548. |
| CapabilityMatrix | Caption 24px / 840px / 2 lines. Option headings 18px / column width minus 24px / 3 lines. Row labels 16px / 216px / 2 lines. Notes 14px / column width minus 64px / 3 lines. Legend 14px / 180px / 2 lines. | Five 62px rows end y=486. Legend starts y=525. Minimum column width is 202px, leaving 138px notes. |
| RejectAndReplace | Criterion 24px / 840px / 3 lines. State label 14px / 216px / 2 lines. Option label 18px / 216px / 3 lines. Rationale 16px / 216px / 4 lines. | Labels start y=325. Reasons start y=420 and stay inside the 304px-tall option panels ending y=514. |
| DecisionFork | Existing accepted ForkLabel word-aware slots, fixed sizes and geometry reused. Existing extreme-width and ordinary-word tests retained. | Two to four branch layouts, including full-length wide-glyph prompt/conditions/outcomes and 32-character scenario/selection labels. |
| TradeoffPivot | Approach 24px / 840px / 2 lines. Side headings 18px / 344px / 2 lines. Points 18px / 336px / 3 lines. Priority 18px / 840px / 2 lines. | Three points per leaf on 72px spacing. Equal 408 x 328 leaves. Priority starts y=548. |

### Approved shared primitive extension

`FitText` and `wrapTextToLines` accept optional `breakLongWords?: boolean`, default false. Strict default behavior is preserved. Opt-in consumers pack ordinary fitting words intact and split only a token wider than its slot into deterministic fixed-font chunks. They still reject unsupported fonts, exhausted explicit line caps and a glyph wider than the slot. The maximum of four lines and supported fixed sizes are unchanged.

The concrete approved consumers are PairedContrast attribute/criterion copy, CapabilityMatrix notes/headings and TradeoffPivot leaf copy. RejectAndReplace also uses the same API for its exact accepted label/rationale bounds. DecisionFork/ForkLabel is unchanged. The shared-scene-library FitText row documents this API.

The complete formal review was read before changes. The exact I1 word-packing examples, I2 accent example and I3 bracket collision were reproduced together before production fixes. Controller authorization permits plain-label hard breaks/tabs to become layout spaces only through an explicit opt-in. This does not modify author input, copy/export data, fixture documents, contracts or the strict default paragraph behavior.

## Fixes and revised layout

| Finding | Root cause | Resulting change and direct coverage |
|---|---|---|
| I1: accepted text crashes | One unbroken maximum token does not cover the less efficient packing of intact fitting words. Hard breaks were treated as mandatory paragraphs in plain-label slots. | Added each exact review probe as a complete schema-valid regression fixture and tested its actual frame150 SVG. Paired alternatives allow 3 lines, criteria/side text 4 lines, with rows on 100px spacing and taller panels. The matrix allows 3-line row labels on 66px spacing. Both rationales use 272px slots, with the rejected panel widened to 296px. All new plain-label FitText consumers explicitly enable `normalizeWhitespace`. |
| I2: accents or emoji separate | Code-point iteration could split a grapheme. Width calculation also charged nonspacing marks, joiners and modifiers as separate visible glyphs. | `Intl.Segmenter` produces grapheme boundaries. Whole-cluster base advances are summed conservatively, excluding nonspacing/enclosing marks, default ignorables and emoji modifiers. Emoji/keycap clusters retain a fallback glyph-width floor. A whole cluster wider than a slot is rejected intact. Tests assert the exact accent-bearing line, whole joined/modifier emoji lines, insufficient-cluster-width rejection and keycap fallback width. No shared width-helper change was needed. |
| I3: criterion looks struck through | The bracket joined both sides with a horizontal segment through the criterion glyphs. | One simultaneously drawn path now contains two side-bracket subpaths, with no center-spanning horizontal stroke. The side strokes remain outside x=408..552, including the full four-line criterion area. A geometry regression checks every rendered bracket segment against its actual criterion text rectangle for default, dense and spaced four-line copy. |

Fixed type sizes and all accepted schema character/collection limits are retained. Fitting ordinary words remain intact. Oversized tokens split only between complete graphemes. The primitive still allows at most four lines, and still rejects line-cap exhaustion or a whole cluster wider than the slot. `normalizeWhitespace?: boolean` defaults false. With it enabled, display layout collapses whitespace to spaces, and the exact original text is retained in the SVG aria label. Strict default newline handling is covered independently and remains unchanged.

The API row in `docs/shared-scene-library.md` documents both opt-in modes. Content-only contracts, public exports, metadata, defaults and binding examples remain unchanged. DecisionFork's accepted renderer/layout was not edited in this fix round.

| Surface | Updated slot and geometry |
|---|---|
| PairedContrast | Alternatives: 20px / 312px / 3 lines. Attributes: 18px / 288px / 4 lines. Criteria: 14px / 144px / 4 lines. Row origins y=274,374,474. Panels end y=554. Comparison band height100 and underline y=row+70 clear the complete attribute text. Caption starts y=572 with 2 lines at 16px. |
| CapabilityMatrix | Row labels: 16px / 216px / 3 lines, first baseline row+19. Row height66, final row ends y=506. Legend first baseline y=548. Existing categorical marks, independent states and focus semantics are retained. |
| RejectAndReplace | Both rationale slots: 16px / 272px / 4 lines. Rejected panel settles at x=156 with width296, spanning x=8..304. Rationale spans x=20..292 and stays within the viewBox and panel. The replacement still occupies the original x=480 slot. |
| TradeoffPivot | Geometry and sizes unchanged. Plain-label normalization explicitly enabled. Added a hard-break regression for every visible input field. |

## Shared packing correction

The old oversized-token branch split each word separately and pushed all chunks as fresh lines. A fitting short prefix and two oversized tokens therefore produced five lines, even though those tokens could use the preceding line's available space. The old paired case had chunk lengths `[1,14,1,14,1]`. Both rationale cases had `[1,15,1,15,1]`.

The shared wrapper now appends an oversized token one complete grapheme at a time into the current last line. Only the first grapheme introduces an inter-word separator, and only when continuing an occupied line. Subsequent graphemes remain adjacent until the slot is full, then continue on the next line. A following word that fits on its own remains atomic: it either fits in the available space or moves whole to a new line. This is a general packing correction, with no special handling for preset IDs, characters or the three reported lengths.

No public API or defaults changed. `breakLongWords` remains opt-in, `normalizeWhitespace` remains opt-in, strict oversized-word rejection and newline behavior remain covered, whole-cluster rejection remains, and the four-line ceiling is retained. Accepted schemas, fixed type sizes, panel/row geometry, marker behavior, bracket timing, metadata, defaults, contracts and collection counts are unchanged.

## Issues

### Critical

### Important

#### I1. Accepted spaced text exceeds the selected line caps and crashes rendering

Primary reference: `src/stock/presets/PairedContrast/ContrastAlternative.tsx:32`. Also see `PairedContrast/ContrastRow.tsx:53`, `CapabilityMatrix/CapabilityRow.tsx:21`, and `RejectAndReplace/SelectionCopy.tsx:60` under the same `src/stock/presets/` root.

The dense fixtures use one unbroken wide token. They prove that token splitting works for that shape, but not that every accepted string fits while ordinary fitting words remain intact. These complete inputs all pass their runtime schemas and then throw `Text cannot fit within the declared line count.` during frame-150 SSR. Each case changes only the named field of that preset's complete default input.

For exact reproductions, define:

```ts
const wideWords = (...lengths: number[]): string =>
  lengths.map((length) => "\u754c".repeat(length)).join(" ");
```

| Preset and field | Exact field value | Accepted length | Slot | Current cap | Required lines |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| PairedContrast `alternatives[0].label` | `wideWords(8, 8, 6)` | 24 of 24 | 312px, 20px type | 2 | 3 |
| PairedContrast `criteria[0].leftText` | `wideWords(8, 8, 8, 7)` | 34 of 34 | 288px, 18px type | 3 | 4 |
| CapabilityMatrix `capabilities[0].label` | `wideWords(7, 7, 6)` | 22 of 22 | 216px, 16px type | 2 | 3 |
| RejectAndReplace `replacement.reason` | `wideWords(7, 7, 7, 7, 7)` | 39 of 42 | 216px, 16px type | 4 | 5 |

The first three required counts were confirmed with `wrapTextToLines` using a four-line allowance. For the rationale, each seven-character word fits independently, but two adjacent words cannot share a line, so five words require five lines. The rejected rationale uses the same slot and has the same defect.

Explicit line breaks are another accepted input shape: PairedContrast `question: "A\nB\nC\nD"` has seven characters, passes its 1..60 schema, and throws because `ContrastHeading.tsx:13` allows three lines. The other string schemas likewise do not exclude line breaks.

**Fix:** choose geometry and wrapping that cover the complete accepted text domain while retaining fixed readable sizes, intact fitting words, every visible character and the approved primitive's four-line ceiling. Handle accepted hard-break inputs deliberately. Do not narrow catalog schemas, clip, truncate or drop copy to make these cases pass. Add focused render regressions for these spaced-word and hard-break cases. The existing boundary tests at `PairedContrast.test.ts:61`, `CapabilityMatrix.test.ts:70`, and `RejectAndReplace.test.ts:69` currently miss them.

#### I2. Oversized-token splitting can detach a combining accent from its letter

Reference: `src/stock/primitives/FitText/FitText.tsx:152`.

`Array.from(word)` iterates Unicode code points, so the new splitting routine can put a line boundary inside one grapheme cluster. This violates the approved requirement to preserve every visible character. A schema-valid PairedContrast criterion label of only ten UTF-16 code units reproduces it:

```ts

wrapTextToLines({

  width: 144,
  fontSize: 14,
  maxLines: 3,
  breakLongWords: true,
});
// Returns ["\u754c\u754c\u754c\u754c\u754c\u754c\u754c\u754ce", "\u0301"].
```

The second line contains only the accent. Joining the line strings back together, as the new test does at `FitText.test.ts:156`, does not detect this visual corruption. Emoji with joiners or modifiers can be divided for the same reason.

**Fix:** split only at grapheme boundaries, with conservative width accounting for each whole cluster. Preserve the strict default and reject a whole cluster that cannot fit rather than breaking it into parts. Add a regression that asserts no line boundary separates the letter/accent pair, plus a joined-emoji case.

#### I3. PairedContrast's bracket crosses its own criterion label

Reference: `src/stock/presets/PairedContrast/ContrastRow.tsx:44`, together with the criterion baseline at `:68`.

The bracket's horizontal segment is at `y - 8`, while the 14px criterion label baseline is `y - 3`. Its stroke therefore passes through the glyph body. I inspected `out/motion/packet-01-layout/PairedContrast-sheet.png`: the default Reader and Handoff labels look struck through, and the same line crosses the first line of each dense criterion. This reduces readability and gives the criterion an unintended rejection treatment.

**Fix:** route the horizontal segment outside the full criterion text bounds, or leave a deliberate gap around those bounds. Keep the paired draw timing and cover the three-line criterion case. Reinspect the default and dense hold stills after the change.

### Minor

None additional within the assigned task scope.

The renderer implementation itself was not rereviewed outside its small diff.

- Drawing components are small, deterministic frame-driven SVG units. No hooks, mutable frame state, renderer aliases to unrelated presets, production service calls or renderer bypasses are introduced.

## Issues

### Critical (Must Fix)

- None found.

### Important (Should Fix)

1. **Consolidate the copied test logic.** `ArgumentBridge/ArgumentBridge.test.ts:28`, `ExceptionDetour/ExceptionDetour.test.ts:28`, `ScopeAperture/ScopeAperture.test.ts:28`, `QualifyApparentConflict/QualifyApparentConflict.test.ts:28`, and `SharedFoundation/SharedFoundation.test.ts:28` contain the same 147-line block through line 174. This consists of the four helpers `_attributes`, `_number`, `_texts`, `_stress` (65 lines), followed by the same four test bodies (82 lines). The repeated common cases account for 20 of the reported 30 tests. The copy/stress helpers drive ten fixture/text cases, while the attribute helpers also support the ten preset-specific semantic/regression cases. Fixes to escaping, enum-field exclusion, stress generation or contract coverage must currently be maintained in five places, which makes these suites prone to drift. The task review rubric treats verbatim logic duplication as Important. Extract one producer-local, test-only helper and parameterized common-case registration, retaining the preset-specific semantic assertions in their own suites. The coordinator can authorize the narrow shared helper path outside the five owned directories. This does not require changing production choreography or shared production APIs.

### Minor (Nice to Have)

1. **A schema-valid topic ID can create an invalid SVG attribute name.** `ScopeAperture/ScopeTopic.tsx:36` places `topic.id` inside the attribute name `data-topic-position-${topic.id}`, while `ScopeAperture/ScopeAperture.schema.ts:10` intentionally accepts any nonempty string up to 20 characters. A focused read-only SSR probe using `id: "topic with space"` passed validation, then emitted `Invalid attribute name: data-topic-position-topic with space`; React dropped that attribute. The drawing and `data-topic` identity remained intact, so this is not a visual failure. Use fixed attributes such as `data-topic`, `data-x` and `data-y` and have tests select by the escaped attribute value. Preserve the catalog's ID bounds rather than narrowing the schema. The coordinator has recorded this for final triage.

2. **The new scope fixture module crosses the review size threshold.** `ScopeAperture/ScopeAperture.fixtures.ts:139` starts a 290-line invalid-input section, bringing the new source file to 428 lines. The Avandar review rules require a split attempt for 401..500 lines. Keep the mandated public fixture path and exports, but reduce the repeated fixture construction or separate private rejection-case data within the owned directory. This is a maintainability issue, not a behavioral failure.

3. **Several new component interfaces miss the repository's React conventions.** Non-union props are accepted intact at `ExceptionDetour/ExceptionDetour.tsx:9`, `QualifyApparentConflict/QualifyApparentConflict.tsx:8`, `ScopeAperture/ScopeAperture.tsx:8`, `SharedFoundation/SharedFoundation.tsx:10`, and `SharedFoundation/FoundationBase.tsx:7`; destructure these parameters. Four-or-more-field inline component shapes at `ArgumentBridge/PremiseStrip.tsx:10`, `ArgumentBridge/PremiseSupport.tsx:13`, `QualifyApparentConflict/StatementContext.tsx:12`, and `SharedFoundation/ApproachTrait.tsx:12` should be named `Props`. Readonly parameter wrappers are missing at `ExceptionDetour/ExceptionCondition.tsx:8`, `ExceptionDetour/ExceptionOutcome.tsx:9`, `ExceptionDetour/StandardOutcome.tsx:5`, and `ScopeAperture/ScopeTopicCopy.tsx:8`. These are consistency changes with no intended rendering change.

4. **Use domain-specific names and existing property helpers.** `ArgumentBridge/ArgumentPremise.tsx:10` uses `count` for the number of premises; name it `numPremises`. `ExceptionDetour/ExceptionDetour.test.ts:213` similarly uses `count` for text-line count. The ID extraction callbacks at `ArgumentBridge/ArgumentBridge.schema.ts:23`, `QualifyApparentConflict/QualifyApparentConflict.schema.ts:24`, `ScopeAperture/ScopeAperture.schema.ts:24`, and `SharedFoundation/SharedFoundation.schema.ts:24` also miss the Avandar `prop` convention. Apply these small convention fixes without changing bounds or semantics.

5. **Prefer undefined for optional JSX branches.** `ArgumentBridge/ArgumentDeck.tsx:30`, `ArgumentBridge/PremiseSupport.tsx:45`, and `ExceptionDetour/RuleGate.tsx:47` add `null` branches although the review rules require undefined when an external signature does not force null. React renders either empty branch identically.

Exit 0 confirmed schema acceptance and captured exactly the invalid-attribute warning described above. No Chromium or MP4 was invoked. No credential file was accessed, printed or copied.

# Motion Atlas Packet 03 implementation report

**Implementation complete. Coordinator specification, code-quality and visual review pending.**

Task base: `21aba3e49`. Worktree: `feat/motion-catalog`.

## Implemented behavior

| Preset | Result |
| --- | --- |
| OfflineLedger | Connectivity collapses at the first entry. Writing continues every 16 frames and each entry presses one matching retained impression into a local drawer. Storage and completed-retention captions wait for their actual beats. Tablet, laptop and notebook casings preserve the same work. |
| JournalReceipts | The accordion journal opens horizontally or vertically. Actual supplied receipts travel from a separate pocket to their referenced entry. Only matched tabs flatten. Zero receipts leave every tab raised. Reordered receipts close the correct identities. |
| PocketInference | A model cartridge seats within a fixed device silhouette. Input, a single cartridge ripple, and a response unfurl stay within the casing throughout the timeline. The changed fixture labels its authored SQL query illustrative and not executed. |
| DisclosureAperture | Every original field remains in place. Only explicitly shared duplicates traverse row-specific apertures into the disclosure envelope. All-retain produces zero copies or openings, and all-share is valid. Metadata-versus-bytes wording is supplied literally. |
| SealedHandoff | Both modes start with a readable brief. Flaps close before travel. A fully opaque cover stays above the intact, unfaded brief throughout transit. Recipient mode unfolds only after arrival. Remain-sealed never reopens after closure. |

Each directory exports its named renderer, strict `inputSchema`, inferred `Input`, `defaultInput`, metadata, fixtures and sixth typed contract assembly. # Spec compliance: Issues found

**🟡 Needs fixes. 0 Critical, 2 Important, 8 Minor findings. Task quality: Needs fixes.**

Reviewed immutable package `review-21aba3e49..1f1ee3933.diff`, base `21aba3e49`, head `1f1ee3933`, against `packet-03-brief.md`, its catalog slice, global constraints and implementation context. The two Important findings affect required choreography. The SealedHandoff clarification permits readable initial contents in both modes and requires concealment after closure. Literal upper-only string bounds permit empty strings.

## Strengths

- All five owned directories contain the six required public modules, strict complete schemas, inferred inputs, defaults, four fixtures, independent semantic assertions and typed contracts. Contract assemblies use `satisfies StockContract<Input>` and structural JSON Schema, for example `OfflineLedger.contract.ts:13` and `DisclosureAperture.contract.ts:13`.
- Catalog metadata, retrieval wording, tags, limitations, distinctions and schema/metadata versions match all five accepted entries. A focused comparison extracted descriptors from the immutable diff and found no mismatch. Defaults and recursive controls preserve the accepted fields and literal bounds, including empty upper-only values in `OfflineLedger.schema.ts:9`, `DisclosureAperture.schema.ts:9` and `SealedHandoff.schema.ts:9`.
- Receipt validation enforces unique existing entry references and collection conservation (`JournalReceipts.schema.ts:37`). Matching uses authored identity, including reordered receipts, rather than row position (`ReceiptHalf.tsx:21`, `JournalTab.tsx:65`). All-retain disclosure produces no copies or apertures (`DisclosureCopies.tsx:9`, `AperturePanel.tsx:19`, `DisclosureAperture.test.ts:41`).
- SealedHandoff keeps the brief painted, covers its full paper with an opaque later element before travel, and opens only after arrival in recipient mode (`EnvelopeFlaps.tsx:8`, `EnvelopeCover.tsx:6`, `SealedHandoff.tsx:13`). Its dense transit test checks actual bounds, opacity and paint order rather than only state markers (`SealedHandoff.test.ts:90`). The coordinator independently observed concealment at frame 80 and readable recipient contents at 150.
- The approved helper extension is test-only. Existing callers retain the same input-text fallback and default frame 150 (`tests/helpers/stockPresetAssertions.ts:66`, `:74`, `:116`, `:129`). Packet 03 expectations derive from authored input and explicit frame conditions, not renderer output (`OfflineLedger.test.ts:73`, `JournalReceipts.test.ts:102`, `SealedHandoff.test.ts:67`). No production helper, registry, license guard, environment, product, database or service mutation appears in the package.

Paths below are relative to `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/`, except where explicitly qualified.

## Critical

None.

## Important

### I1. PocketInference never establishes the required empty socket

**Location:** `PocketInference/ModelCartridge.tsx:8`, `:23`, `:34`.

**Requirement:** “Open on a fixed device cutaway with an empty cartridge socket. Seat a compact labeled model cartridge in the socket.”

**Reproduction:** Default input, frame 18, `showCutaway: true`. A focused SSR probe found socket `x=194, y=122, width=572, height=88` and the fully painted cartridge `x=202, y=106, width=556, height=72`, including its model label. The cartridge already overlaps 56 pixels of the socket vertically. This is also its position for every frame before 20. The only seating movement is 24 pixels, from y106 to y130, so no readable setup frame ever shows an empty socket. The later inference sequence is present, but its required initial installation state is missing.

**Fix:** Establish a genuinely empty setup socket, then introduce and seat the cartridge within the device before input/inference. Add a before/after test that checks the actual painted installation geometry or visibility. The existing tests check containment and the later ripple, not the empty setup (`PocketInference.test.ts:21`, `:43`, `:66`).

### I2. Vertical receipt halves appear outside the canvas

**Location:** `JournalReceipts/ReceiptHalf.tsx:31`, `:33`, `:39`.

**Requirement:** Both fold-direction variants must implement authored receipt halves emerging from the separate acknowledgment pocket, with readable text and supported fixed layout bounds in the 960 x 600 viewBox.

**Reproduction:** Set `foldDirection: "vertical"` on default input and seek to frame 60. A focused SSR probe found the first fully opaque receipt at `translate(800 280)`, with width 260, ending at x1060. The canvas ends at x960. Every later receipt starts with the same 100-pixel overflow at frame `60 + index * 12`. The horizontal variant's 150-pixel half fits that anchor. Dense vertical input also places its maximum-length label slot at global x810 through x1050, so text can be cut off as each receipt appears. These frames are absent from the coordinator's 18/80/150 sheet samples.

**Fix:** Keep the entire vertical receipt and its text within the canvas at emergence and throughout travel, with a direction-aware pocket/starting anchor. Add a focused vertical early-transit bounds assertion using the actual receipt geometry, including dense labels. The current geometry test samples only the final frame (`JournalReceipts.test.ts:40`).

## Minor

1. **M1. The dense journal's documented resolved beat starts before resolution.** `JournalReceipts/JournalReceipts.metadata.ts:100` declares the completed state held from frame 108, while `ReceiptHalf.tsx:29` starts receipt five at 108, arrives at 128, and `JournalTab.tsx:68` flattens its tab through 136. Compress the stagger to the documented hold or describe the real supported timing. Add a dense decisive-frame assertion so metadata and maximum collection behavior remain aligned.

2. **M2. The new disclosure metadata module exceeds the review size threshold.** `DisclosureAperture/DisclosureAperture.metadata.ts:155` starts a separable controls section in a 421-line authored source file. Avandar's review rules require a split attempt at 401 to 500 lines. Extract the controls into a clearly owned nested module while preserving the required public metadata module, or document a concrete reason a split cannot improve the structure. There is an identifiable retrieval-copy/control seam here.

3. **M3. New guards omit required braces.** Examples include `DisclosureAperture/AperturePanel.tsx:19`, `:21`, `DisclosureAperture/DisclosureField.tsx:30`, `JournalReceipts/ReceiptHalf.tsx:33`, `OfflineLedger/LedgerImpression.tsx:19` and the schema refinements at `DisclosureAperture/DisclosureAperture.schema.ts:32`, `JournalReceipts/JournalReceipts.schema.ts:39`, `OfflineLedger/OfflineLedger.schema.ts:30`, `SealedHandoff/SealedHandoff.schema.ts:33`. Apply braces consistently to the new guards, including multiline conditions.

4. **M4. Multiple new docstrings exceed the 80-character rule.** Examples: `DisclosureAperture/DisclosureField.tsx:15`, `JournalReceipts/JournalEntryText.tsx:5`, `OfflineLedger/LedgerEntry.tsx:13`, `PocketInference/ModelCartridge.tsx:6`, `SealedHandoff/HandoffBrief.tsx:6`. Wrap the long member docstrings across short lines without changing their meaning.

5. **M5. Two local helpers appear after their exported callers.** `JournalReceipts/JournalEntryText.tsx:31` defines `_createLabelsFromEntry` after its use at line 16. `JournalReceipts/JournalTab.tsx:60` defines `_getClosingProgress` after its use at line 22. Move the helpers above their callers per the review readability convention.

6. **M6. New helper interfaces use positional multi-argument inputs.** `JournalReceipts/getJournalGeometry.ts:4` adds a three-argument public helper instead of the required RO-RO input object. The private helpers at `JournalReceipts/JournalTab.tsx:60`, `JournalReceipts/JournalEntryText.tsx:31` and each metadata module's `_message` at line 7 have the same convention issue. Use descriptive object inputs where the signature is locally owned. The shared test helper's mandated `render(frame, input)` callback is an external contract for these consumers and is excluded from this finding.

7. **M7. New tests iterate data collections with imperative loops.** Examples: `DisclosureAperture/DisclosureAperture.test.ts:22`, `:73`, `:95`, `JournalReceipts/JournalReceipts.test.ts:22`, `:41`, `OfflineLedger/OfflineLedger.test.ts:41`, `PocketInference/PocketInference.test.ts:22`, `:101`, `SealedHandoff/SealedHandoff.test.ts:22`, `:91`, `:125`. Replace collection iteration with `forEach` or another declarative operation. These small synchronous fixture/toggle arrays do not meet the documented exceptions. Numeric frame stepping is not the basis of this finding.

8. **M8. The reported React Doctor output contains a warning.** `JournalReceipts/JournalReceipts.schema.ts:48` uses repeated array membership lookup and the implementation report records `react-doctor/js-set-map-lookups`. At no more than five entries and receipts, this is negligible runtime cost and does not undermine correctness. It remains a reported validation warning under the task reviewer contract. Reuse a Set for membership if retaining a pristine diagnostic run is the desired policy. No suppression or broad optimization is warranted.

## Verification and scope

- Read the complete immutable diff in sequential passes. No Git commands or test suites were rerun. The implementation report records 69/69 affected Packet 02 and Packet 03 checks, both TypeScript projects, formatting and whitespace checks passing on this head. Those are reported results, not newly executed suite claims.
- Ran the existing license guard successfully through `REMOTION_KEYS_FILE`, without reading or printing credentials. Ran one focused SSR command for the two concrete doubts above. It exited 0 and printed the actual socket/cartridge geometry and receipt right edge, confirming I1 and I2. Ran a diff-only metadata/version comparison for all five accepted entries, with no mismatches.
- The shared helper's diff hunks cut off the containing functions and omitted their recursive input walkers. Read `apps/ava-video-producer/tests/helpers/stockPresetAssertions.ts` once to judge the named cross-cutting risk: whether the approved extension preserved Packet 02 fallback behavior and independently derived expectations. It does. No other changed source file was read separately from the package. No unrelated source was inspected.
- Coordinator evidence is static SSR/rsvg inspection of all five default/dense sheets at frames 18, 80 and 150 under `out/motion/packet-03-early/1f1ee3933/`. Reported observations include no final text clipping/overlap, correct receipt matching/pending tabs, transient disclosure duplication at the aperture, and sealed transit concealment. This supports those sampled states, not all-frame bounds or live playback.

## Cannot verify from this diff

- Central registry wiring, omitted-input default resolution, generated catalogs/bundles, preservation of all earlier presets and final collection/count totals span later integration. The contract modules provide the intended imports but do not prove registry behavior. Coordinator should resolve these at Task 7.
- The outer opaque envelope, seam thresholds, accent/background propagation and final 1280 x 800 six-second delivery depend on unchanged shared rendering and the final composition. This packet sets `loopFrames: 180` but does not establish final export behavior.
- Live gallery playback, browser rendering, serial Chromium visual review, final MP4 inspection and frame-gate output remain Task 7 gates. No Chromium render or MP4 was run in this review. The static sheets cannot substitute for those gates.

## Assessment

**Spec compliance: Issues found. Task quality: Needs fixes.** The authored contracts and semantic separations are strong. The missing empty-socket setup and clipped vertical receipt emergence require corrections and focused regression coverage before this packet can be accepted.

## Next Actions

| # | Owner | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Codex | Fix I1 and I2 in the owned preset directories, add focused regression assertions, and address the Minor findings in scope. |
| 2 | Coordinator | Review the correction diff and retain decisive vertical-receipt and initial-socket visual evidence. Resolve the listed Task 7 gates at integration. |
| 3 | Pablo | No action required. Convenience copies: `~/Downloads/avandar_motion-catalog/motion-atlas-packet-03/packet-03-review.md` and `packet-03-review.pdf`. |

## Delivered behavior

| CustodyTransfer | Receiver contact precedes acknowledgement at 72..80. One responsibility marker crosses during 80..100. Sender support withdraws during 100..120. Waiting retains sender support and responsibility. All three object shapes physically touch the common support at y=376. | 11 passed |
| ReadinessLatch | Stable array spatial order, workUnits-based completion during 24..112, ready pins withdraw over the next eight frames, and every false ready value retains its pin. Release begins at 122 only when every participant is ready and reaches its final point by 146. Completed ribbons touch the latch and remain mounted. | 9 passed |
| ContributionWeave | Vertical tension finishes before the first horizontal pass. Each weft sweeps once during 36..60, 60..84 or 84..108. Actual clipped crossing patches alternate their visible owner, and weaveStart reverses the construction. Every contributor retains one identifiable end when enabled. | 10 passed |
| ExpiringLease | Exactly one referenced participant holds one token initially. Collar segments drain at equal editorial intervals during 36..108. At 108 participant ownership ends, and the token retracts to neutral custody during 108..136. No successor is inferred. | 8 passed |
| DashboardSlotAssembly | Differently sized panels reveal during 12..40 inside their reserved regions. The feature docks during 40..64, then supporting panels dock during 64..88, 76..100 and 88..112. Scope settles and guides withdraw during 112..130. Completed geometry holds through 166. | 9 passed |

All components consume GraphicProps and a schema-inferred complete Input. The existing StockGraphic supplies the 960 x 600 viewBox, opaque ground, 180-frame envelope, 30 fps and 1280 x 800 delivery. No shared envelope, frame gate, registry, product source, generated catalog or bundle was edited.

## Content contracts

Each owned directory exports its named component, `inputSchema`, inferred `Input`, `defaultInput`, `fixtures`, `metadata`, and a descriptive camelCase contract with `satisfies StockContract<Input>`. The contract includes complete structural JSON Schema, runtime-only semantic rules, recursive serializable controls, indexed defaultTextPaths, the complete accepted binding example, collection and version fields.

Schemas and controls preserve exact catalog bounds. IDs with only an upper bound accept the empty string, and unique collections allow at most one such ID. holderId and featuredWidgetId must match their respective collections. Dashboard titles and lines accept empty strings. Value widgets require exactly one line. Holder names must differ, and weave IDs must be unique across both axes. Supplied data is never silently merged with defaults, omitted, counted separately or reinterpreted as calculated metrics.

Content modules import only content/schema modules and type contracts. They do not import any renderer. Public metadata retains catalog titles, descriptions, intent, tags, goodFor, distinctions and limits, without private source provenance. Controls use serializable translation descriptors, including the readiness timing clarification. Every renderer-visible label comes from its supplied input or numeric values. No new untranslated authored frontend sentence was introduced in JSX.

## RED/GREEN evidence

The test/fixture modules were written before each animation implementation. An empty renderer established a behavioral RED for each preset after the content modules were assembled. The first CustodyTransfer invocation also demonstrated that the missing renderer import failed before a real empty-renderer behavioral RED was run. Schema rejection fixtures passed once their strict schemas were present. This is renderer semantic RED/GREEN evidence, not a claim that each schema predicate was independently mutation-tested.

| Preset | Observed empty-renderer RED | GREEN and additional evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CustodyTransfer | 2 passed, 5 failed. Missing sender support, responsibility and visible copy. | 11 passed. A later physical-contact regression first failed with actual bottom 356 versus required support 376, then passed after all silhouettes touched the support. |
| ReadinessLatch | 2 passed, 5 failed. Missing branch pins, work geometry, shared gate and copy. | 9 passed. A later contact regression failed with completed ribbon end 640 versus latch 650, then passed in both orientations after the horizontal/vertical ribbons reached their respective gate lines. |
| ContributionWeave | 2 passed, 5 failed. Missing contributor ends, alternating patches, shuttle geometry and copy. | 10 passed. Includes unequal 2x3 and 3x2 contributor arrays and two render namespaces. |
| ExpiringLease | 3 passed, 4 failed. Missing initial ownership, finite segments and supplied copy. | 8 passed. The initial geometry loop had no elements under the empty stub. It was strengthened to assert four sockets and one token before checking coordinates. |
| DashboardSlotAssembly | 2 passed, 6 failed. Missing panels, featured reassignment, fixed text, guides and copy. | 9 passed. The full text stress found an 18px value label packing into five lines in the narrowest top-layout slot. A fixed 16px value treatment, unchanged across frames, satisfies the accepted domain. |

Each preset reused the reviewed shared helper for strict schema rejections, complete content contracts, default/minimum/dense/changed fixtures, deterministic forward/backward seeks, and text packing, whitespace and whole grapheme stress. Custody holder fields are excluded from common stress mutation because identical generated names correctly violate distinct-holder semantics. Separate local tests independently exercise and assert both holder slots with distinct wide, inefficiently packed, embedded-break and combining/ZWJ inputs. Readiness and dashboard common stress exercise both orientations/layouts at state-relevant frames.

Producer commands ran from `apps/ava-video-producer`. The license guard consumed the existing documented key-pair path through REMOTION_KEYS_FILE. The file and credentials were never opened, printed or copied.

# Spec Compliance

- ❌ **Issues found.** The five requested preset directories and complete content contracts are present, but ReadinessLatch does not make its result cross the latch, and DashboardSlotAssembly omits the distinct loose-panel setup that its assembly sequence requires. Exact findings I1 and I2 follow. The dense custody seal also touches authored detail text (M1).
- Reviewed immutable task range: base `7e753392e`, head `ac0c76e5be92727bf481c4d5e205730ea324ad50`, using `review-7e753392e..ac0c76e5b.diff`. Its 58 additions stay inside the five owned preset directories. No source, index, HEAD, branch, registry, generated artifact, service, or database was changed by this review.
- ⚠️ **Cannot verify from this diff:** the final 170-entry registration and 106/64 split, omitted-entire-input default dispatch, central parser/envelope behavior, live gallery operation, final 1280 x 800 / 30 fps delivery, MP4 rhythm, seam/frame-gate results, and serial-render/license behavior. These belong to coordinator integration/Task 7 and final render evidence. Each local contract declares `loopFrames: 180` (`ContributionWeave.contract.ts:18`, `CustodyTransfer.contract.ts:18`, `DashboardSlotAssembly.contract.ts:18`, `ExpiringLease.contract.ts:18`, `ReadinessLatch.contract.ts:18`), but a declaration alone does not verify the delivered composition.
- ⚠️ **Cannot establish live SVG gate disappearance from the supplied raster samples:** the default/dense frame-150 PNGs still display the ReadinessLatch gate although the SVG uses `pathLength=1` and a dash offset of 1. Coordinator should verify the corrected opening in the actual delivery renderer. I1 does not depend on that renderer question: the result is geometrically downstream before opening in the source itself.

All source locations below are relative to `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/` unless another prefix is shown.

## Strengths

- **Complete, renderer-free content boundaries.** Each `.contract.ts` assembles the schema, structural JSON Schema, semantic rules, defaults, fixtures, recursive controls, indexed text paths, binding example, versions and collection with `satisfies StockContract<Input>` (`ContributionWeave/ContributionWeave.contract.ts:13`, `CustodyTransfer/CustodyTransfer.contract.ts:13`, `DashboardSlotAssembly/DashboardSlotAssembly.contract.ts:13`, `ExpiringLease/ExpiringLease.contract.ts:13`, `ReadinessLatch/ReadinessLatch.contract.ts:13`). Their imports point to content modules and the contract type, without a renderer import.
- **Accepted domains are preserved.** Strict nested schemas enforce bounded collections, distinct holders, cross-axis weave uniqueness, holder references, featured references and single-line value widgets. Upper-only IDs, titles and widget lines accept empty strings (`CustodyTransfer/CustodyTransfer.schema.ts:5`, `ContributionWeave/ContributionWeave.schema.ts:3`, `ExpiringLease/ExpiringLease.schema.ts:4`, `ReadinessLatch/ReadinessLatch.schema.ts:4`, `DashboardSlotAssembly/DashboardSlotAssembly.schema.ts:4`). Fixtures deliberately include empty IDs and empty dashboard text (`DashboardSlotAssembly/DashboardSlotAssembly.fixtures.ts:34`).
- **Custody sequencing has real physical and behavioral evidence.** Recipient contact completes before acknowledgment, responsibility traverses during 80..100, and sender support withdraws during 100..120. Waiting retains the sender's support and marker. All three silhouettes end at the common y=376 support (`CustodyTransfer/CustodySupport.tsx:16`, `CustodyTransfer/CustodyTransfer.tsx:13`, `CustodyTransfer/CustodyObjectShape.tsx:4`, `CustodyTransfer/CustodyTransfer.test.ts:66`, `:111`, `:161`, `:212`).
- **Readiness timing follows the coordinator clarification.** Work quantities determine completion and the next eight frames withdraw ready pins, while input array order fixes positions and false readiness retains its pin (`ReadinessLatch/ReadinessRibbon.tsx:30`, `ReadinessLatch/ReadinessLatch.test.ts:108`, `:130`). This correctly resolves the obsolete catalog sentence about array-order withdrawal.
- **The weave actually alternates painted ownership.** Clipped crossing patches select the visible contributor, changing `weaveStart` reverses that selection, and the components retain distinct bands/ends. Tests include unequal axis counts and two render namespaces with valid unique fragments and resolved URL references (`ContributionWeave/WeaveCrossing.tsx:21`, `ContributionWeave/WeaveShuttle.tsx:39`, `ContributionWeave/ContributionWeave.test.ts:68`, `:90`, `:142`, `:157`). Authored IDs remain attribute values rather than generated attribute names or fragment IDs.
- **Lease conservation is explicit.** The one token follows the referenced holder until expiry at 108, then retracts to neutral dock (480,430) by 136. No successor is inferred. Collar count comes from the authored lifetime and drains at equal intervals (`ExpiringLease/ExpiringLease.tsx:25`, `ExpiringLease/LeaseSocket.tsx:35`, `ExpiringLease/LeaseCollar.tsx:11`, `ExpiringLease/ExpiringLease.test.ts:74`, `:114`).
- **Dashboard data and typography remain separate.** Feature reassignment changes actual slots, all supplied widget identities survive, and panel geometry changes without a scale transform on text. Font sizes remain fixed and the dense test measures actual tspan baselines within moving panels (`DashboardSlotAssembly/getWidgetRectFromInput.ts:10`, `DashboardSlotAssembly/DashboardWidgetPanel.tsx:24`, `DashboardSlotAssembly/DashboardWidgetContent.tsx:22`, `DashboardSlotAssembly/DashboardSlotAssembly.test.ts:92`, `:112`, `:208`).
- **The test structure is appropriately scoped.** All five suites reuse `registerStockPresetAssertions` and supply input/timeline-derived text oracles, with semantic tests remaining local. Custody independently stresses distinct holder slots rather than violating holder uniqueness through the shared mutation helper (`CustodyTransfer/CustodyTransfer.test.ts:25`, `:43`, `:142`; `ReadinessLatch/ReadinessLatch.test.ts:24`, `:54`; `ContributionWeave/ContributionWeave.test.ts:27`, `:34`; `ExpiringLease/ExpiringLease.test.ts:28`, `:43`; `DashboardSlotAssembly/DashboardSlotAssembly.test.ts:27`, `:34`).

## Issues

### Critical (Must Fix)

None found.

### Important (Should Fix)

#### I1. Readiness result begins beyond the closed gate and never crosses it

**Locations:** `ReadinessLatch/ReadinessGate.tsx:24` and `:32`. Related coverage: `ReadinessLatch/ReadinessLatch.test.ts:118`, `:159`. Related label placement: `ReadinessLatch/ReadinessCaptions.tsx:16`.

The required sequence is a blocked result, every required branch finishing and withdrawing its pin, the latch opening at 122, then a labeled result passing through it by 146. The current horizontal gate is at x=650, but even the blocked result has center x=680 and radius 12: its entire disk is already to the right of the gate. Release only moves x=680 to x=830 along y=526, which is the bottom endpoint of the gate. In vertical orientation the gate is y=400, but the blocked disk begins at y=420 with radius 12 and only moves farther down to y=505. Thus neither orientation depicts crossing the barrier, including the authored blocked-dependency case. The action text remains a static caption at y=60 rather than labeling a result that passes through the opening.

The existing tests assert these downstream initial coordinates and final coordinates without comparing the result's side to the gate, so they stay green through the missing physical story. The supplied `ReadinessLatch-sheet.png` confirms the default result below/beyond the line in both pre-release and released samples.

**Fix:** place the held result on the upstream side and release it through an actual gate opening after all pins withdraw. Give the released result its supplied action label in the relevant geometry. Add assertions comparing the full result bounds with the barrier before/after release in both orientations, including an unready participant that never crosses. Verify opening visibility in the delivery renderer instead of treating a dash-offset number as proof of an opening.

#### I2. Dashboard panels are already composed before the assembly beat

**Locations:** `DashboardSlotAssembly/getWidgetRectFromInput.ts:35`, `:46`, `:60`. Related coverage: `DashboardSlotAssembly/DashboardSlotAssembly.test.ts:142`.

The brief requires frames 12..40 to establish loose, differently sized information panels and an empty dashboard outline, followed by the featured panel docking first and the other panels reshaping into the available slots during 40..112. Instead, setup rectangles are computed directly from each widget's final assigned slot. The feature starts only 24px inset (8px vertically for feature-top); every support starts only 16px or 8px inset horizontally and 4px vertically, with width 16px smaller and height 4px smaller. They already occupy the final hierarchy, arrangement, order and reserved regions before frame 40. Docking is a slight expansion of an already composed dashboard. The default frame-18, frame-90 and frame-150 stills make the missing loose-to-composed transformation visible.

**Fix:** author a distinct readable loose-panel setup and a perceptible path into the eventual slots, preserving input identities and fixed font sizes. Keep the required final slots non-overlapping. The current test imposes the stronger condition that every panel remains inside the board and non-overlapping during every sampled transition. That is an implementation assumption, not the brief's final-slot constraint, and should not silently restrict the correction to tiny in-slot growth. Update the setup/trajectory tests to protect the actual requested sequence, with canvas/readability checks and final non-overlap. Temporary overlap during travel is a choreography choice, not a missing requirement to enforce.

### Minor (Nice to Have)

#### M1. Accepted custody seal touches the first dense detail line

**Locations:** `CustodyTransfer/CustodyAcceptance.tsx:12`, `CustodyTransfer/CustodyObject.tsx:6`, `:34`.

The acknowledgment seal is centered at (680,230), radius 22, with a 2px stroke, so its painted bottom reaches y=253. The first detail begins at x=534 with a 14px font and baseline y=260, placing the top of its glyphs around y=250. Maximum-width detail text spans the seal's x position. The supplied `CustodyTransfer-dense-150.png` shows the lower seal edge touching/overpainting the first row of Ws. The semantic handoff remains clear, so this is local typography polish rather than a reason by itself to reject the task.

**Fix:** reserve a clear vertical gap between the seal and the adjoining details, and assert non-occlusion against their actual text rows. A focused accepted 28-character recipient probe also produces three holder-name lines with baselines 165, 188.4 and 211.8, so preserve room above the seal as well when choosing its revised position.

## Evidence and focused checks

- Read the task brief, catalog, global constraints, implementation context, implementer report and immutable task diff in per-preset passes. The initial unfiltered diff output was truncated because this package uses numbered source blocks rather than unified `diff --git` headers. Remaining blocks were read through the existing package's file headings. No changed source file was read separately.
- Independently inspected existing coordinator outputs only: `apps/ava-video-producer/out/motion/packet-04-early/ac0c76e5b/CustodyTransfer-dense-150.png`, `DashboardSlotAssembly-sheet.png` and `ReadinessLatch-sheet.png`. These are static review evidence, not live browser or MP4 approval. No Chromium or new image/video render was run.
- **Named risk: custody seal versus accepted text packing.** Read the unchanged shared `src/stock/primitives/FitText/FitText.tsx` to establish actual baseline semantics (`<tspan>` increments are font size times 1.3), then ran one focused `pnpm exec tsx -e` SSR probe. Input recipient used the CJK character U+754C repeated 8 times, a space, 9 times, a space, and 9 times. It is exactly 28 characters, passes the strict schema, and renders three lines at y=165/188.4/211.8. This probe supports placement review without changing schemas or rendering through Chromium. No other outside-diff source inspection was needed.
- The implementer reports 47/47 focused tests passing, both source/tools TypeScript checks clean, license guard exit 0, and the red/green semantic history. These results were read, not rerun. The missing crossing and assembly sequences are visible in source and existing stills, so repeating passing checks would not resolve them.
- React Doctor evidence is honestly limited to one scan of 58 files with eight warnings. Source inspection is consistent with the reported moves of static objects and fixed role/caption identities. The retained positional custody detail key (`CustodyTransfer/CustodyObject.tsx:36`) represents immutable authored display slots containing duplicate-capable primitive strings and no local state, so it is a verified low-impact diagnostic false positive here. This review does not claim a clean rescan. The producer suites/types were not rerun, no broader branch scan was performed, and no subagents were dispatched.

## Assessment

**Task quality: Needs fixes.** The packet has clean scoped modules, strict content contracts, useful semantic tests and strong identity/conservation handling. Two required motion stories remain unimplemented in actual geometry, and their current tests encode the mistaken geometry rather than protecting those sequences.

**Spec compliance: Issues found. Task quality: Needs fixes.**

Reviewed immutable task diff `46e4af45d03b1bc4fdc967d6509162031ae0f154` to

accepted catalog, global constraints and implementation context. Paths below are

## Spec compliance

- The five requested preset directories contain their required components,
  schemas, defaults, metadata, fixtures, semantic tests and complete typed
  contract modules. The contracts use schema-inferred inputs and
  `satisfies StockContract<Input>`, including JSON Schema, semantic rules,
  recursive controls, indexed copy paths and full binding examples. Examples:
  `src/stock/presets/CellNormalization/CellNormalization.contract.ts:16` and

- The FitText extension is explicitly authorized by the brief. Its implementation
  changes the maximum cap from four to eight, with no wrapping or font changes.
  Seven/eight-line acceptance, nine-line capacity rejection and content overflow
  rejection accompany the inventory update:
  `src/stock/primitives/FitText/FitText.tsx:43`,
  `src/stock/primitives/FitText/FitText.test.ts:352` and
  `docs/shared-scene-library.md:164`. This is not a scope violation.

  lanes, and the default chart treatment omits the requested focal context

## Strengths

- Pipeline insertion is a physical change rather than a state marker. Existing
  modules separate before the parked module descends, and final connectors use
  adjacent module bounds and final authored order:

## Issues

### Critical

None found.

### Important

**I1. Comparison headings label the wrong content.**

`src/stock/presets/CellNormalization/CleanupHeadings.tsx:11` hard-codes the result
heading above the left lane and the original heading above the right lane for
both comparison modes. But
`src/stock/presets/CellNormalization/CleanupRowCopy.tsx:15` puts retained originals

does not apply.

**M2. Geometry file names do not match their single main exports.**

`src/stock/presets/PipelineStepSplice/spliceGeometry.ts:5`,
`src/stock/presets/ProvenancePeelback/sourceSheetGeometry.ts:11` and
`src/stock/presets/ReportPageBind/reportPageGeometry.ts:5` each export one geometry
function whose name differs from its file name. Rename each file to its main
export and update the local imports, following the module checklist. These
helpers are otherwise appropriately small and local to their owning presets.

- Named risk: the new long provenance blocks rely on a conservative width model.

## Cannot verify from this task diff

## Assessment

**Task quality: Needs fixes.** The packet has distinct geometry, strict accepted
contracts and meaningful semantic tests. I1 makes the central comparison

## Important findings

### 1. Conflict decision marks identify the rejected lane

**Evidence:** `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/FieldConflictChoice/ConflictChoiceMark.tsx:30`, `:33`, `:45`; `getConflictCandidateState.ts:34` and `ConflictFieldHeading.tsx:31` in that same directory.

At resolution, every chosen value moves to x=44 and every retained alternative to x=500. The selection bracket instead ends at `44 + sourceIndex * 456`. Choosing source index 1 therefore brackets the rejected value at x=500, or an empty lane when alternatives are hidden. The `Selected` heading is also fixed at x=500 for every resolved field, even though its result is on the left. This contradicts the explicit source choice and makes the two decision styles communicate different ownership. The coordinator's `FieldConflictChoice-selection-bracket-150.png` visibly confirms both cases.

**Fix:** Derive bracket/rail endpoints and selected-label placement from the actual chosen panel position, including its movement. Keep unresolved review status associated with the unresolved pair. Add assertions that the bracket and selected caption belong to the chosen result for both source indices and with alternatives shown/hidden. The existing `FieldConflictChoice.test.ts:92` checks only that a mark exists, so it cannot catch this error.

### 2. Duplicate comparison-pair labels detach from the records they describe

**Evidence:** `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/DuplicateReviewStack/DuplicateDecisionLabels.tsx:27`, `:28`, `:40`, `:42`; `getDuplicateCardLayout.ts:30`, `getDuplicateGroupLayout.ts:18`, and `DuplicateGroupHeading.tsx:30` in that same directory.

In comparison-pair mode, cards occupy x=`30 + recordIndex * 300`, but `Retained example` stays at the group x=30. When the second record is retained, as in `DuplicateReviewStack.fixtures.ts:99`, the caption sits above the first, unretained card. The alternatives caption is placed at the group x and y+142, below all cards. For the first group at frame 150 its baseline is y=334, immediately beside the next group's bracket at y=335. The coordinator's `DuplicateReviewStack-comparison-pair-150.png` consequently reads as if the following unresolved group owns that alternatives caption. Both labels need clear ownership of the supplied retained/alternative identities.

**Fix:** In comparison-pair mode, anchor role labels to the corresponding card or an unambiguous region inside that group's bounds. Reserve space so an alternatives label cannot collide with or appear to introduce the next group. Test each retained index with two and three records, two groups, and unresolved groups. `DuplicateReviewStack.test.ts:102` checks only card bounds/disjointness, leaving role-label ownership unprotected.

### 3. Private SVG test parsers omit the required helper prefix

The new non-exported top-level helpers `cards`, `cells`, `rows`, `slips`, and `items` lack the repository's `_` prefix: `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/DuplicateReviewStack/DuplicateReviewStack.test.ts:53`, `FieldConflictChoice/FieldConflictChoice.test.ts:51`, `KeyedRowZipper/KeyedRowZipper.test.ts:26`, `NestedDrilldownWindow/NestedDrilldownWindow.test.ts:50`, and `QueueRelief/QueueRelief.test.ts:17`. # Motion Atlas packet 08 implementation report

**Ready for independent review. Five renderers and complete content contracts are committed. Serial visual review remains with the coordinator.**

- Branch: `feat/motion-catalog`.
- Exact task base: `1bfa1edcbdd2e41372bc8d22c6a3c9d640507235`.
- Implementation commit: `fecb96d81f9e40d3a4cd415188f0811ec12f2f8b`.
- Scope: 52 files, 5,014 inserted lines, all under `apps/ava-video-producer/`.
- No registry, generated catalog, product, service, database, environment or license-guard changes. No Chromium, video rendering, publication, push or merge.

## Implemented behavior

| Preset | Distinct physical behavior and tested semantics |
| --- | --- |
| FeedbackRefinement | One draft crosses between author and reviewer. Its authored note returns visibly tethered to the draft. Clip geometry wipes original text into the supplied revision. One or two sequential rounds retain exact revision continuity. Notes physically detach into optional reserved trail slots. |
| WorkDecomposition | A continuous slab receives travelling ruled cuts. Both strips and alternating cuts preserve every supplied effort share and total rectangle area. Pieces translate without resizing, remain disjoint at hold, and retain parent membership. External labels cover the smallest pieces. |
| PriorityInsertion | An existing numbered queue opens exactly one slot. Only its chosen suffix shifts one position. The incoming item follows a vertical then horizontal side spur. Every existing item retains relative order for every insertion position. |
| UncertaintyUnfold | Two sleeves unfold from a fixed point to supplied endpoints on one fixed linear ruler. The optional reference lowers at its original value. Null references and point/endpoint equality are accepted. Extreme finite spans retain central zero and finite geometry. |
| LinkedParameterRehearsal | Direct affine output pointers move with the source, hold a trial and return to exact baseline values. Only nonzero multipliers have mechanical couplings. Zero-multiplier outputs remain fixed. Every sampled pointer uses the actual rule, including intermediate frames and finite overflow-cancellation cases. |

All content modules remain renderer-free. Each preset exports its named renderer, strict inferred input schema, complete fictional default, fixtures, typed contract, public metadata, structural JSON Schema, semantic rules, recursive serializable controls, explicit indexed default-text paths, full binding example and accepted versions. Metadata retains catalog intent, distinction and limits without private provenance.

## Executed RED and GREEN evidence

Tests were written before each implementation. Each initial renderer was importable and returned null. These were executed assertion failures, not missing-module failures. Schema definitions and rejection fixtures already loaded in these initial runs, so schema rejection was GREEN while renderer behavior was RED. This distinction is intentional and explicit.

| Suite | Initial executed RED | Initial GREEN | Final focused GREEN |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FeedbackRefinement | 1 passed, 2 failed. Both geometry tests failed with `The actual travelling draft must be drawn`. | 3/3 | 9/9 |
| WorkDecomposition | 1 passed, 2 failed. Original slab assertion failed; both partition outputs were empty. | 3/3 | 9/9 |
| PriorityInsertion | 1 passed, 2 failed. Rendered queue lengths were 0 instead of 5. | 3/3 | 9/9 |
| UncertaintyUnfold | 1 passed, 2 failed. Actual estimate-point and interval-band geometry assertions failed. | 3/3 | 7/7 |
| LinkedParameterRehearsal | 1 passed, 2 failed. Output pointer count was 0 instead of 3; the actual source-pointer assertion failed. | 3/3 | 8/8 |
| Shared finite-range helpers | 0 passed, 4 failed. Constant-zero scaffolding violated exact endpoints and failed to reject invalid domains. | 4/4 | 4/4 |

A second test-first refinement run covered physical details: 21 passed and 3 failed across the first three suites. Feedback lacked a moving note rectangle, the incoming queue item moved diagonally instead of following its spur (`340 !== 580` at the turn), and travelling cut lines were absent (`0 !== 2`). After implementing these details, that run passed 24/24. Later text and per-frame bounds coverage brought the final focused total to **46/46**, with no skipped or todo tests.

The first FeedbackRefinement GREEN run produced React SVG namespace warnings because its test rendered a bare SVG group. Wrapping the server-render test in an SVG root removed the warnings. Final runs contain no such warnings.

## Commands and checks

Producer commands ran from `apps/ava-video-producer/`. Before the initial focused runs and final validation, the documented license consumer ran successfully:

```sh
REMOTION_KEYS_FILE=/Users/juanpablosarmiento/src/avandar/apps/ava-video-producer/.env.local \
  node scripts/require-license.mjs
```

No credential file was opened, printed or copied. Each initial RED and initial GREEN used its exact preset command, for example:

```sh

  src/stock/presets/FeedbackRefinement/FeedbackRefinement.test.ts
```

The corresponding exact file paths were used for WorkDecomposition, PriorityInsertion, UncertaintyUnfold and LinkedParameterRehearsal. Final focused validation ran these five files and both helper files together:

```sh
pnpm exec tsx --test \
  src/stock/presets/FeedbackRefinement/FeedbackRefinement.test.ts \
  src/stock/presets/WorkDecomposition/WorkDecomposition.test.ts \
  src/stock/presets/PriorityInsertion/PriorityInsertion.test.ts \
  src/stock/presets/UncertaintyUnfold/UncertaintyUnfold.test.ts \
  src/stock/presets/LinkedParameterRehearsal/LinkedParameterRehearsal.test.ts \
  src/stock/numeric/normalizeFiniteRange/normalizeFiniteRange.test.ts \
  src/stock/numeric/interpolateFiniteRange/interpolateFiniteRange.test.ts
```

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` | Exit 0. |
| `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.tools.json` | Exit 0. |
| Scoped ESLint over five owned preset directories and `src/stock/numeric/**/*.ts` | Exit 0 after fixing duplicate test imports and one shadowed test variable. |
| `git diff --cached --check` | Exit 0. |
| Final focused unit tests | 46 passed, 0 failed. |

Exactly one React Doctor invocation ran from the repository root, with the dispatched base:

```sh
CI=1 pnpm exec react-doctor --yes --scope changed \
  --base 1bfa1edcbdd2e41372bc8d22c6a3c9d640507235 --no-score
```

It scanned **51 changed source files**, exited 0 and reported one `react-doctor/no-array-index-as-key` warning in FeedbackRefinement. The note key was changed to `round.draft`, which is unique under the enforced two-round continuity and changed-revision rules. Focused tests and scoped lint passed after that fix. Doctor was not rerun, and no score-service retry occurred. Its recorded output was one warning, not a clean scan.

## Coverage and limits

The shared independent test helper covers default, minimum, dense and changed fixtures, strict invalid documents, complete contracts/bindings, backward seeks, inefficient wide-word packing, embedded whitespace and grapheme clusters. Preset-local tests protect actual SVG coordinates, rectangle areas, path movement, clip widths, optional state and independent numeric relationships.

- Work item and queue IDs retain the accepted upper-only bounds, including empty IDs and empty references when that ID exists. Linked output IDs retain their explicit nonempty 1..20 bound. Space/Unicode IDs remain values of fixed attribute names.
- Work area tests assert actual rectangle areas against input effort fractions in both layouts. Final rectangles are disjoint. Dense rectangles stay within the enclosing reserve throughout separation.
- Queue tests cover every insertion point, exact suffix shifts and all intermediate dense item bounds.
- Uncertainty tests preserve fixed point/reference positions, endpoint equality, null reference and extreme finite-span normalization.
- Linked tests compare actual dependent values and pointer coordinates against affine rules over 133 normal frames per fixture, verify exact trial and restored holds, and check all 180 frames for the extreme and cancellation fixtures.
- Typography stays fixed and uses reviewed FitText behavior. Ordinary labels normalize whitespace for layout while original input and aria text remain unchanged. Oversized tokens split only at whole grapheme boundaries.
- Numeric calculations use IEEE-754 values. Finite inputs are not arbitrarily magnitude-capped. Results retain normal floating-point rounding and underflow limits; the renderer is not arbitrary-precision arithmetic. Authored equations and scenarios are not empirical evidence or causal inference.
- Natural-language agreement of feedback, priority captions, interval meaning and interpretation remains the author's responsibility. Structural and numeric invariants are validated; prose truth is not inferred.
- Unit/SSR geometry tests are not Chromium stills, visual approval or frame-gate evidence. Those remain outstanding coordinator checks.

## Approved clarifications and shared scope

The coordinator explicitly approved these two concrete scope decisions during implementation:

1. Positive gaps cannot preserve all slab material inside an identical filled outline. The original contour therefore remains a thin fixed reference at its exact initial bounds. A distinct enclosing bracket with visible reserve exists from setup. Pieces translate into that reserve without resizing or duplicate filled material.
2. Both numerical presets need finite-range normalization, and the linked preset needs safe interpolation. Two renderer-free helpers were added with tests and one shared-scene-library API inventory row.
