# Motion Atlas packet 21 implementation report

**Source and Important-review corrections committed. Static verification passes. Controller visual acceptance remains pending.**

Latest correction: `b07546a9d6d9b10edc9f4a31327274990cf16297`. The original implementation evidence below remains historical; correction-round evidence is appended at the end.

Commit: `22e2e4e83104a409fb4e0382730206d7df7029a6`  
Branch: `feat/motion-catalog`  
React Doctor base: `865bff9346174203a881b1fbe274b653a00e89b5`  
Recorded: 2026-10-17

## Scope and contract

Five independent configurable SVG animations were added in 66 files, exclusively inside the five owned preset directories. Registry integration, browser rendering, frame gates, MP4 review and acceptance belong to the controller. No shared code, dependencies, product components, registry, databases or services changed. No source edits followed the final verification run or Doctor scan. The scoped source commit was made before report preparation so fresh review could begin immediately.

Every preset exports its named renderer, inferred Input, strict runtime inputSchema, complete fictional default, four fixtures (default, minimum, dense, changed), metadata, recursive serializable controls and a renderer-free typed contract. Each contract uses satisfies StockContract<Input>, a structural JSON Schema, semantic rules, explicit indexed defaultTextPaths and binding examples. Inputs remain complete documents. Collection lengths drive geometry. No text classifier interprets authored prose; prose meaning, fictional framing and conceptual agreement remain the author's responsibility.

All packet IDs have explicit 1..16 bounds in this catalog. No upper-only ID field was narrowed. Minimum fixtures retain legal whitespace and Unicode identities; dense fixtures use unique 16-character IDs with valid references. Authored strings are retained. The selected datasets/rows caption reuses the existing localized option descriptor. Other scene prose comes from the authored input. Charge source captions follow controller ruling 43: invoice/reference 1..32, five key captions 1..16, outcome/difference 1..32, review/example 1..52. A boundary test accepts 32 and rejects 33 before the renderer implementation.

## Distinct behavior and physical checks

| Preset | Implemented behavior and geometry evidence |
|---|---|
| SchemaColumnEvolution | Existing columns slide left and an added column opens from the seam. Earlier values and IDs remain exact; each earlier added value is missing. One later row enters, including a null value. Visible header rectangles share the seam and reach width 260. Dense text stays inside row bodies. The later caption waits until the incoming row clears its rail. |
| PluginCapabilityInstall | One utility moves into one socket, retaining the source strip. Install derives one tally mark per retained record and integer-scaled category bars. Defer leaves the empty socket and no tally. Empty categories keep labels, including all eight records concentrated in one category. Actual utility transforms, record identities, marks, bar widths and heading clearance are asserted. |
| ChargeReferenceAlignment | Literal key windows align or retain mismatch notches. Four exact strings plus quantity gate comparison; every independent mismatch suppresses difference geometry and number. Matched rulers use one physical zero and domain for zero, equal, positive and negative differences. Full-length literal values fit source windows; wrapped source captions and currency clear the numeric rulers. |
| WorkspaceCapacityExtension | The same tray extends; existing tabs remain at identical positions. Expand reveals only the visible part of each added slot, then seats every request. Keep leaves all requests pending even with spare current capacity. Actual slot x+width stays within the moving tray edge. Dense tab labels stay inside moving tabs and clear captions. Zero-width extra slots are omitted. No clip, mask or defs IDs are introduced. |
| EqualCountUnequalVolume | Equal-cardinality shelves align their count marks, then unfold exact bytes/common-scale strips. Zero-byte items retain identity tabs and count membership. Three display units and both toggles preserve exact widths and totals. Actual strip widths are checked against bytes/scale, with a shared zero. The first total clears the second title; text clears byte strips. |

All renderers consume frame-driven shared motion primitives. They use fixed readable type and LabelSlots/FitText, shared palette and the outer StockGraphic envelope. No replacement generic scene renderer was added. The local text-envelope helper is test-only and explicitly limited to the untransformed markup used by its assertions. Shared test helpers separately walk transforms for canvas bounds. No new shared primitive/API was required.

## Genuine initial RED and first GREEN

Before renderer behavior, each preset had strict structural fields, default/minimum/dense/changed fixtures, rejection fixtures and its semantic test. Each initial renderer was an importable, callable React component returning null. Failures were observable missing semantic output, never missing imports. Cross-field refinements were then implemented along with the scene. Original raw outputs are in the evidence directory.

For each NAME below, both RED and first GREEN used this exact producer-cwd command:

```sh
pnpm exec tsx --test src/stock/presets/NAME/NAME.test.ts
```

Charge ruling 43 was resolved during this initial RED stage. Its added boundary test passed while behavior remained RED: tests 4, pass 3, fail 1, exit 1. Files NAME-red.log, NAME-green1.log and ChargeReferenceAlignment-ruling43-red.log retain complete output. The additional initial failures for the other four presets were their cross-field rejection cases, not fixture construction failures.

## Actual test chronology after first GREEN

These expanded tests were added after the initial semantic GREEN and should not be mistaken for the initial test-first cycle. The table is chronological. Logs preserve full diagnostic output, including failures and observer corrections.

## Final commands and outputs

# Packet 21 specification and quality review

**Spec compliance: Issues found. Task quality: Needs fixes.**

Counts: 0 Critical, 2 Important, 5 Minor. This is a task-scoped review of the immutable packet, not final Motion Atlas acceptance.

Base: `865bff9346174203a881b1fbe274b653a00e89b5`  
Head: `22e2e4e83104a409fb4e0382730206d7df7029a6`  
Review date: 2026-10-17

Source references below are relative to `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/`. The supplied package contains 66 new files and 8,244 inserted lines. I read it once, consecutively in bounded sections, without rereading changed files or running Git commands.

## Spec compliance

The five presets implement their distinct structured-input semantics, collection bounds, strict nested objects, authored choices, deterministic frame timing, and renderer-free contracts. Two gaps remain: the capacity decision is absent from default localization paths, and its pending caption visually labels the existing tray. The transient header overflow and tiny-unit rounding are quality findings, not rejected input domains.

- **SchemaColumnEvolution:** `SchemaColumnEvolution.schema.ts:4`, `EvolutionRow.tsx:26`, `LaterEvolutionRow.tsx:19`, and `SchemaColumnEvolution.test.ts:108` preserve prior IDs/values, missing historical values, one later row, and the hidden-caption/null variant. Added-header containment needs polish.
- **PluginCapabilityInstall:** `PluginCapabilityInstall.schema.ts:44`, `UtilitySocket.tsx:9`, `CategoryTally.tsx:23`, `TallyMarks.tsx:20`, and `PluginCapabilityInstall.test.ts:112` implement one utility, unchanged records, derived counts, empty categories, and no deferred tally.
- **ChargeReferenceAlignment:** `ChargeReferenceAlignment.schema.ts:4`, `getComparisonFromInput.ts:11`, `AmountRuler.tsx:26`, and `ChargeReferenceAlignment.test.ts:126` enforce exact comparison eligibility and signed arithmetic. Source captions honor ruling 43.
- **WorkspaceCapacityExtension:** `WorkspaceCapacityExtension.schema.ts:47`, `CapacityTray.tsx:9`, `CapacitySlots.tsx:19`, `PendingResources.tsx:8`, and `WorkspaceCapacityExtension.test.ts:108` preserve existing tabs and complete-request choice semantics. Caption association and default localization need fixes.
- **EqualCountUnequalVolume:** `EqualCountUnequalVolume.schema.ts:45`, `ByteItem.tsx:22`, `VolumeTotal.tsx:13`, and `EqualCountUnequalVolume.test.ts:91` preserve equal counts, unique IDs, unequal exact totals, zero-byte membership, common basis, and unit-independent widths. Tiny labels can round to zero.

Every preset has the six required component/schema/metadata/fixtures/test/contract files. Additional controls and focused components remain within the five owned directories. Each contract at line 16 contains a typed `satisfies StockContract<Input>` assembly, structural JSON Schema, semantic rules, versions, fixtures, controls, binding examples, and collection. The collection split in this packet is four general and one social-sector. No unrelated implementation changes appear in the package.

## Strengths

- Runtime constraints match the accepted numeric, collection, identity and reference domains. They do not trim authored strings, classify prose, silently backfill earlier values, truncate capacity demand, or reject valid unresolved charge contexts. See the five schema references above.
- Tests go beyond diagnostic attributes: charge rulers inspect actual x/width (`ChargeReferenceAlignment.test.ts:182`), installation inspects the socket/body (`PluginCapabilityInstall.test.ts:112`), capacity checks the moving boundary (`WorkspaceCapacityExtension.test.ts:94`), and byte strips check a real shared zero and exact widths (`EqualCountUnequalVolume.test.ts:91`).
- Short scene components separate choreography from schema/metadata content. Optional captions do not erase the underlying states: `EvolutionRowBackdrop.tsx:31`, `ResourceTab.tsx:42`, and `CategoryTally.tsx:34` retain the relevant visual cues.

## Important findings

### I1. The capacity decision bypasses default copy localization

**Location:** `WorkspaceCapacityExtension/WorkspaceCapacityExtension.metadata.ts:197`.

`defaultTextPaths` lists the resource, allowance and framing prose but omits `["choice", "label"]`. The default sentence is displayed by `WorkspaceCapacityExtension.tsx:32`; it is authored display copy, not an identifier or enum. The existing message collector and default resolver iterate only these paths, so registration and catalog generation cannot extract or translate this sentence. Add the missing indexed path and a focused assertion that the decision has a default message and is translated when resolving a default, while supplied authored input remains unchanged.

### I2. The pending caption labels the existing tray

**Location:** `WorkspaceCapacityExtension/PendingResources.tsx:14`.

The pending caption is fixed at `(80, 212)`, immediately over the existing tray starting at y=220. The requests sit at y approximately 419 without a connector or pending-group outline. In the default frame-36 image, “Requested resources” therefore heads the three existing resources; the two actual requests are unlabeled. This persists on keep and confuses retained work with pending demand, especially when names are hidden. Move the caption beside the requests or connect it explicitly. Assert the association and seating clearance for default and hidden-label keep scenes.

## Minor findings

### M1. Added-header text escapes the unfolding boundary

**Location:** `SchemaColumnEvolution/EvolutionHeader.tsx:37`.

The whole 230-unit label slot fades with `expansion`, while the enclosing header width is only `260 * expansion` at line 28. In the dense frame-36 image, the first wrapped line extends approximately 28 units beyond the header edge. The text stays readable and does not cover unrelated content, so this is transient containment polish. Delay the label reveal until it fits, or reveal it within the actual moving boundary without shrinking type. The current seam test at `SchemaColumnEvolution.test.ts:108` checks endpoint rectangles, not moving text containment.

### M2. Tiny positive measurements become indistinguishable from zero in labels

**Location:** `EqualCountUnequalVolume/buildByteLabel.ts:12`.

Fixed two-decimal KiB/MiB formatting makes one byte and zero bytes both read `0.00`; a one-byte scale maximum also reads `0.00` at the end of a full positive strip. This is visible in both supplied zero-byte-item unit variants. The catalog explicitly permits rounded decimals, and exact byte geometry is correct, so this is not an arithmetic/spec blocker. Preserve useful magnitude with adaptive precision, an exact-byte companion, or an authored/localized approximation convention. Keep the selected unit and common scale intact.

### M3. Retained React Doctor index-key warning

**Location:** `ChargeReferenceAlignment/ChargeRulers.tsx:18`.

The reported `no-array-index-as-key` warning remains. The two stateless positions always mean invoice then reference, so there is no demonstrated identity bug. Named source keys would remove the warning and document that stable meaning. No Doctor rerun was performed.

### M4. Retained React Doctor static-value warning

**Location:** `ChargeReferenceAlignment/ContextWindows.tsx:8`.

The reported `prefer-module-scope-static-value` warning remains for the fixed field/caption tuple. Five entries have negligible runtime cost and are not effect dependencies. Moving the tuple to module scope is a small maintainability improvement. No Doctor rerun was performed.

### M5. Four new fixture modules are oversized and heavily repetitive

**Locations:** `ChargeReferenceAlignment/ChargeReferenceAlignment.fixtures.ts:163` (447 total lines), `EqualCountUnequalVolume/EqualCountUnequalVolume.fixtures.ts:231` (656), `PluginCapabilityInstall/PluginCapabilityInstall.fixtures.ts:211` (524), and `WorkspaceCapacityExtension/WorkspaceCapacityExtension.fixtures.ts:203` (533).

Invalid cases repeat complete unchanged defaults for single-field changes. This adds review and maintenance cost and exceeds the repository review skill's source-size thresholds. These are data modules rather than duplicated production algorithms, so severity is Minor. Preserve the required fixture exports and complete resolved documents while reducing repeated data or organizing the independent cases into an internal directory module. Retain each case's observable rejection purpose.

## Evidence and review limits

The implementation report records genuine initial RED results for each semantic test, followed by GREEN; later text and geometry failures are separately identified. Its final claim is 63/63 tests, both TypeScript checks, scoped ESLint/Oxfmt/diff checks, and one Doctor run with two warnings. I assessed the test source and report; I did not rerun these gates, Doctor, browser sessions, Chromium rendering, or movies. The controller independently supplied a clean-source and canonical-fingerprint check; this review does not relabel that as an independent reviewer check.

Named checks outside the diff:

1. **Missing default-copy extraction risk:** inspected `src/stock/i18n/stockCopyMessages.ts:58` and `src/stock/i18n/resolveStockCopy.ts:65`. Both enumerate only the declared paths. This confirms I1's localization impact.
2. **Coverage overstating physical/layout guarantees:** inspected the two directly imported test helpers. `tests/helpers/stockPresetAssertions.ts:103` verifies contract structure but not completeness of default text paths. The layout helper checks canvas bounds, not semantic caption association. These checks explain why I1/I2 and M1 can survive the reported suite; they are not new findings against unchanged helpers.
3. **Controller-named visible risks:** inspected four existing PNGs from the exact reviewed commit, without regenerating them: dense schema frame 36, default capacity frame 36, and zero-byte volume KiB/MiB frame 150. They substantiate I2, M1 and M2. They are SSR/rsvg evidence, not browser/MP4 acceptance.

Cannot verify from this packet diff: central registry wiring; generated Lingui catalogs and browser localization; complete-input fallback at the central entry point; the final 170-export/count split; outer 960x600/1280x800 envelope, 180-frame/30-fps delivery and unchanged frame-gate thresholds; final browser/raster/MP4 quality; and cross-packet retrieval distinctions. These belong to the later assigned integration and validation gates and remain unclaimed. The original demo/product adapters, licensing consumer and public registry are untouched in this package.

Its `:6` normalizer implements ruling45 without rewriting inputs. `DraftRelation.tsx:7` derives direction from supplied endpoints; `AttributeAttachments.tsx:10` derives the owner connection. `DraftReview.tsx:25` gates acceptance on the supplied outcome. All five named renderers, inferred Input types, schemas, defaults, fixtures, metadata, controls and typed contracts are present. Author text passes through unchanged; no natural-language classifier or live inference was introduced. Each component uses authored arrays and shared frame helpers, with the outer scene still responsible for the envelope.

## Issues

### Critical

None.

### Important

**I1. Keep the source sentence visible while phrase copies lift.** `UtteranceToModelDraft/DraftSlip.tsx:29` starts every moving socket at the source fragment's x coordinate and 15 pixels above its baseline. `PhraseSocket.tsx:20` immediately gives the copy an opaque 254-by-96 rectangle, and `UtteranceToModelDraft.tsx:24` paints the source before the model. Other short, adjacent source fragments also start overlapping cards. This breaks the accepted source-preserving choreography, and retaining text in aria attributes does not make it visible. Move phrase copies through a clear layer/route, delay the opaque socket body until clear of the sentence, or otherwise preserve the source and unmapped connector words. # Motion Atlas Packet 23 review

**Spec compliance: Issues found. Task quality: Needs fixes.**

Reviewed `74ed4389ef84aec8eed7614266284a6342d89ef5` through
`90feb5ff7c7c343762aded75827dd65b49114d82`. This task-scoped review contains
**0 Critical, 5 Important and 2 Minor findings**. The five accepted scene
domains and core state transitions are implemented, but four visible
presentation defects and duplicated control-generation logic require changes.

Source references below are relative to
`apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/`. Evidence paths are relative to
the worktree unless explicitly identified as producer paths.

## Strengths

- **Exact structured domains:** the strict schemas preserve catalog bounds,
  nested key rejection and authored prose. Expertise references and distinct
  expert IDs are checked in `ExpertiseRoleExchange/ExpertiseRoleExchange.schema.ts:28`.
  Recognition focus is checked in
  `PeerContributionRecognition/PeerContributionRecognition.schema.ts:24`.
  Release owner/due fields permit empty strings except for open follow-ups,
  as required, in `ReleaseRepairObligations/ReleaseRepairObligations.schema.ts:3`
  and `:43`. No language classifier or inferred outcome was introduced.
- **Distinct physical scenes:** tool exchange, attribution pointing, chair
  transport, pipe repair, and gated delivery have separate renderers.
  Semantic tests compare actual SVG coordinates: expertise hand/tool contact
  at `ExpertiseRoleExchange/ExpertiseRoleExchange.test.ts:41` and `:148`,
  recognition pointing at
  `PeerContributionRecognition/PeerContributionRecognition.test.ts:41`,
  chair transport at `SupportRequestResponse/SupportRequestResponse.test.ts:204`,
  seal insertion at `RecurringLeakPrevention/RecurringLeakPrevention.test.ts:154`,
  and artifact containment in its destination at
  `ReleaseRepairObligations/ReleaseRepairObligations.test.ts:41`.
- **Retained semantics:** only joins adds a chair, every open blocker holds
  delivery, and successful leak retests retain the normal outlet flow.
  Relevant implementations are `SupportRequestResponse/SupportParticipants.tsx:9`,
  `ReleaseRepairObligations/ReleaseRepairObligations.tsx:15`, and
  `RecurringLeakPrevention/LeakPipe.tsx:7`.
- **Renderer-free contracts:** each contract imports only content modules
  and contract types, supplies recursive serializable controls, complete
  structural JSON Schema, semantic rules, binding input, versions and
  explicit indexed default-copy paths. Representative assembly:
  `ExpertiseRoleExchange/ExpertiseRoleExchange.contract.ts:86`.
  All five defaults and binding examples match their accepted catalog entries.
- **Bounded source scope:** the immutable package contains 42 additions only
  in the five assigned directories, with 5,006 inserted lines. Each required
  six-file module is present, and the largest file is 384 lines. No registry,
  generated bundle, shared envelope, gate, product source or license code is
  changed by this packet.

## Important findings

### I1. Contribution labels cross the acknowledgment bubble

**Files:** `PeerContributionRecognition/RecognitionObjects.tsx:19` and
`PeerContributionRecognition/RecognitionExchange.tsx:49`.

The contribution-label baseline is 145 with 16px text, while the acknowledgment
box extends from y=55 through y=143. Consequently the first line of each
contribution label lies across the bottom border and partly inside the box
once the acknowledgment appears. This happens with the supplied default and
dense layouts, not only exceptional authored copy. The main renderer paints
the objects after the exchange at
`PeerContributionRecognition/PeerContributionRecognition.tsx:23`, so the text
is visible but visually collides with an unrelated statement container.
This violates the readable-copy requirement and weakens the link between an
object and its label.

Reserve separate vertical regions for the acknowledgment and object captions,
including all accepted wrapped lines. Add a geometric clearance assertion
between their painted bounds. The controller's dense frame 150 was inspected:
producer `out/motion/packet-23-early/90feb5ff7/PeerContributionRecognition-dense-150.png`.

### I2. The response tail intersects the colleague's name

**Files:** `SupportRequestResponse/SupportParticipants.tsx:64` and
`SupportRequestResponse/SupportWords.tsx:43`.

The colleague's 20px name starts at baseline y=200. The response tail spans
y=181..199 at x=765..795, inside that first line's occupied region. With the
accepted dense 18-character name, the triangle crosses the glyphs throughout
the response and hold. Paint order keeps the name on top, but does not remove
the visible collision. Participant identity must remain clearly readable.

Move the tail or name slot to maintain clearance for every supported wrapping
case, and assert the actual first-line bounds against the tail. The controller's
dense frame 150 was inspected: producer
`out/motion/packet-23-early/90feb5ff7/SupportRequestResponse-dense-150.png`.

### I3. An unperformed retest is captioned as an illustrated retest

**File:** `RecurringLeakPrevention/RecurringLeakPrevention.tsx:21`.

After frame 107, `phase` unconditionally becomes `input.labels.test`. Therefore
`retest: "not-tested"` with `showPhaseCaptions: true` displays the default
"Illustrated retest" beside "Not retested". The outlet correctly remains
paused, but the phase caption describes an action the scene intentionally did
not perform. This is a structured-state selection error, not a demand to
interpret or rewrite arbitrary author prose.

For the untested branch, retain an accurate repair phase or omit the nonexistent
test phase while preserving the final untested observation. Add an assertion
that the test-phase copy is not presented as performed in this branch.
The controller's configured sheet at frames 90, 120 and 150 was inspected:
producer `out/motion/packet-23-variants/90feb5ff7/90-120-150/RecurringLeakPrevention/tighten-not-tested-with-phase-captions/RecurringLeakPrevention-tighten-not-tested-with-phase-captions-sheet.png`.

### I4. Five copies of the same recursive controls algorithm

**Files:** each preset's `.contract.ts`, beginning at line 14 (the duplicated
`JsonNode` type) and line 24 (`_control`). Specific anchors:
`ExpertiseRoleExchange/ExpertiseRoleExchange.contract.ts:24`,
`PeerContributionRecognition/PeerContributionRecognition.contract.ts:24`,
`SupportRequestResponse/SupportRequestResponse.contract.ts:24`,
`RecurringLeakPrevention/RecurringLeakPrevention.contract.ts:24`, and
`ReleaseRepairObligations/ReleaseRepairObligations.contract.ts:24`.

All five modules copy the same enum, boolean, collection, nested-object and
text conversion blocks. Only the message namespace and the two reference-select
overrides differ. This duplicates roughly 50 lines of branching behavior per
contract, including unreachable collection branches in the two collection-free
schemas. Changes to recursive editing behavior now require synchronized edits
in five places. The task-reviewer rubric explicitly treats verbatim duplicated
logic as Important.

Use one renderer-free converter with a namespace and reference-select overrides,
coordinated with the controller because shared files are outside the worker's
owned paths. Alternatively, use explicit per-scene serialized control data
within the owned paths. The required contract exports do not require duplicated
conversion algorithms. A focused inventory of the existing contracts directory
found no dedicated controls converter to reuse; no broader source crawl was done.

### I5. Register connectors do not visibly originate at their issue tabs

**Files:** `ReleaseRepairObligations/RepairRegister.tsx:30`,
`ReleaseRepairObligations/ReleaseArtifact.tsx:38`, and
`ReleaseRepairObligations/ReleaseRepairObligations.tsx:43`.

Every connector begins at `artifactX + 150`, inside the artifact, although
the actual tab spans `artifactX - 8` through `artifactX + 17`. The register is
painted before the opaque artifact, so the connector's origin and most of
its route disappear behind the artifact. In the dense frame 65, the lines
emerge from a common lower edge and horizontal route, with no visible
connection to the four separate numbered tabs. That loses the required
tab-to-matching-register unfolding relationship during frames 41..90.

Route each connector from its actual visible tab or notch boundary to its
matching entry, and preserve that origin through paint order. The regression
at `ReleaseRepairObligations/ReleaseRepairObligations.test.ts:174` only checks
the source y coordinate; add x/contact and visibility assertions. The
controller's retained dense frame 65 was inspected: producer
`out/motion/packet-23-early/90feb5ff7/50-65-80/ReleaseRepairObligations/ReleaseRepairObligations-dense-65.png`.

## Minor findings

### M1. Participant stress tests promise more than their assertions establish

**Files:** `PeerContributionRecognition/PeerContributionRecognition.test.ts:199`
and `SupportRequestResponse/SupportRequestResponse.test.ts:192`.

The tests claim whole graphemes and fixed text slots, but only assert that the
full original string occurs in `aria-label`. An SVG could split a grapheme,
drop visible characters, change its font size or overlap the name and still
pass. These participant fields are excluded from the generic stress mutation,
so those helpers do not fill this gap for the locally supplied strings.
Assert rendered text/tspan content, grapheme boundaries and the intended text
geometry, or narrow the test names to their actual accessibility-text claim.

### M2. The retained Doctor warning is not a pristine diagnostic run

**File:** `ExpertiseRoleExchange/ExpertiseRoleExchange.tsx:52`.

The retained scan reports a non-null assertion on the expert lookup
(`.temp/packet-23/react-doctor.log:27`; logged source line 50 precedes the final
type-only Props declaration). Schema validation proves every accepted expert
references one of exactly two people, so this is a high-confidence false
positive for valid contract input, not a demonstrated runtime failure.
It is recorded because the reviewer contract requires diagnostic noise to remain
visible. A schema-aware typed lookup or explicit invariant handling can remove
the warning without suppressing the rule or changing the accepted domain.

## Verification and evidence limits

- The full immutable diff was read once in consecutive bounded sections.
  Only its header was reread because aggregate tool output had truncated that
  header. No changed source file was separately reread, and no branch history
  was reconstructed.
- The retained final runtime log records **67 tests, 67 passing, 0 failing** at
  `.temp/packet-23/covering-tests.log:68`. Read-only inspection also confirmed
  real earlier failures for missing geometry, hand/tool contact, seal contact,
  connector y origin, wrapped-row clearance and chair contact. The reported
  names of earlier logs are not used as evidence of success.
- `format-check.log` reports correctly formatted files. `lint-final.log`,
  `ts-source.log`, `ts-tools.log` and `diff-check.log` are empty, consistent
  with the implementer's reported exit-zero checks. The files themselves do
  not independently encode process exit status. The Doctor log confirms one
  warning and 42 scanned files. No tests, compiler, lint, Doctor or motion
  rendering were rerun for this review.
- The retained manifest lists the same 42 owned source paths and fingerprint
  `c5a53154eb27bbb3941df4a19c269d83dcbcb19c72cedad484a0ab23af2be1d6`.
  This review verifies the immutable diff and retained record; it does not
  independently reconstruct the historical fingerprint computation.
- Named uncertainty: whether the shared test registrars establish cross-element
  clearance and full recursive controls coverage. A focused read of
  `tests/helpers/registerStockTextLayoutAssertions/registerStockTextLayoutAssertions.ts`
  and `tests/helpers/stockPresetAssertions.ts` confirmed canvas bounds,
  deterministic seeks, supplied copy, top-level control paths and bindings.
  They do not establish general shape/text occlusion or deeply inspect each
  nested control. Source inspection establishes the packet's recursive controls.
  No finding is assigned to unchanged helper code.
- Controller observations were assessed against source and four retained
  preview images. They support I1-I3 and I5; they are not substituted for whole-loop
  motion or final export acceptance. No browser or composition render was run.

## Cannot verify from this packet

- The final 150-addition count, 86/64 additions split, preserved initial subset,
  and final 106/64 split require the controller's cross-task registry audit.
- Gallery registration, generated localization extraction, browser controls,
  omitted-input default resolution, custom accent/background integration and
  1280 x 800 delivery are outside this diff. This packet leaves their shared
  implementations unchanged; direct component and content tests cannot prove
  end-to-end integration.
- Opaque envelope/seam behavior, actual font metrics across delivery platforms,
  every variant over every frame, serial MP4 exports, unchanged frame-gate
  acceptance and final visual approval remain controller gates.
- Historical license-consumer invocation and process exit statuses are reported
  evidence, not independently replayed actions. No credentials or environment
  file were opened, printed or copied during this review.

## Assessment

**Task quality: Needs fixes.** Core semantic behavior, accepted domains and
evidence are substantial. Fix the four visible presentation problems and the
duplicated contract algorithm before accepting Packet 23. The two Minor items
are distinct coverage/diagnostic concerns.

## Artifact verification

The authoritative review is this SDD file. The Downloads Markdown is an exact
copy. Conversion with `markdown-to-pdf` produced a six-page PDF. Every page
was rendered with Poppler and visually inspected for clipping, overlapping
text, broken glyphs and table layout. No artifact-layout defect was found.

| # | Owner | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Codex | Address I1-I5 and consider M1-M2 within the agreed ownership boundaries. |
| 2 | Controller | Verify fixes, complete variant inspection and retain cross-task integration/export gates. |
| 3 | Controller | Read the synchronized artifacts: `~/Downloads/avandar_motion-catalog/motion-atlas-packet-23/packet-23-review.md` and `~/Downloads/avandar_motion-catalog/motion-atlas-packet-23/packet-23-review.pdf`. |

# Motion Atlas Packet 24 implementation report

Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS. Five implemented presets are ready for fresh review;
serial browser/render QA and registry integration remain controller-owned.

- Base: `b08d3be504fa1a05026797bad514dba8beb79b55`
- Immutable HEAD: `356caae65e88b14acab20b731086393e40d9b49b`
- Commit: `feat(video): add Motion Atlas packet 24`
- Source diff SHA-256: `fa2f429c7b71389face6e344b7dcd15e3e06e2cfd444e2682e83f7d8a13f9ffe`
- Scope: 62 new files, 5,514 lines, exclusively the five owned preset directories.
- No registry, shared API, generated catalog, product, environment, or database edits.

## Implemented behavior and bounds

| Preset | Behavior and accepted bounds |
| --- | --- |
| SharedJigPreparation | One formed two-hole or corner guide visits 1..3 existing workpieces in input order. Marking/carrying hands contact the actual guide; all marks and the retained guide remain. Both material and alignment variants are authored. |
| PortableWorkTransfer | 1..4 originals stay anchored. Each same-ID copy packs into one rigidly carried folio. Accepted opens and places copies; awaiting-open retains its opaque cover and exterior label manifest without successful use. |
| ServiceablePanelSwap | One targeted slot among 2..4 opens, moves its original to a retained tray, receives a distinct replacement, then closes. Unaffected modules keep exact IDs and positions for every first/last/interior target. |
| SchemaPlanLocalExecution | 2..6 unique local rows, finite values 0..100. Only supplied schema/question copy travels out; a plan returns. Equality selection and sum produce 5 for defaults, 10 after the supplied category edit. Hidden rows retain exact membership. |
| QueryColumnCacheGrowth | 2..5 columns with equal 2..5 cell occurrences; cells allow empty strings and <=16 characters. Covered request hits, second request adds missing columns to one cache. Existing columns stay fixed; new source columns append. Both B occurrences remain. |

Every catalog string limit, required field, enum, unique ID, reference, and
cross-field condition is retained in strict Zod schemas and JSON Schema plus
explicit semantic rules. Supplied prose is preserved; no English classifiers
or inferred factual claims were introduced. All default prose paths have
extraction/resolution tests. IDs, literal cell values and category keys remain
authored data rather than translated prose.

Each directory contains its named renderer, schema, metadata, fixtures, test,
and typed contract. Narrow private components keep handling, shapes, labels,
and frame geometry local. The first three contracts use createStockControls;
the final two reuse supported subobjects plus explicit number/primitive-array
controls. Primitive reference controls use the empty item path and root scope.

## TDD chronology and retained evidence

All five complete default/minimum/dense/changed fixture sets and rejection
sets existed before their callable semantic RED. Each renderer was a callable
null scaffold. Fixture validation passed and the actual semantic assertion
failed; no missing-module failures are counted as behavioral RED.

Commands below run from `apps/ava-video-producer`. The license command used
only the documented consumer, never opened or printed the credential file:

```sh
REMOTION_KEYS_FILE=/Users/juanpablosarmiento/src/avandar/apps/ava-video-producer/.env.local node scripts/require-license.mjs
pnpm exec tsx --test src/stock/presets/SharedJigPreparation/SharedJigPreparation.test.ts
pnpm exec tsx --test src/stock/presets/PortableWorkTransfer/PortableWorkTransfer.test.ts
pnpm exec tsx --test src/stock/presets/ServiceablePanelSwap/ServiceablePanelSwap.test.ts
pnpm exec tsx --test src/stock/presets/SchemaPlanLocalExecution/SchemaPlanLocalExecution.test.ts
pnpm exec tsx --test src/stock/presets/QueryColumnCacheGrowth/QueryColumnCacheGrowth.test.ts
```

| Cycle | Original RED | First semantic GREEN |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jig | 2 tests, 1 pass, 1 fail; `0 !== 1` (guide count) | 2/2 |
| Portable | 2 tests, 1 pass, 1 fail; `0 !== 1` (retained identity) | 2/2 |
| Service | 2 tests, 1 pass, 1 fail; `assert.ok(before)` | 2/2 |
| Schema | 2 tests, 1 pass, 1 fail; `assert.ok(outbound)` | 2/2 |
| Cache | 2 tests, 1 pass, 1 fail; `0 !== 1` (single cache) | Semantic assertion passed in 6/9 run; 3 text capacity failures remained |

Evidence root: `.temp/feat-motion-catalog/packet-24/`.
The first three RED outputs and first Jig/Portable GREEN outputs were tool
outputs, not saved full logs. `early-red-excerpts.txt` contains verbatim
relevant historical RED excerpts. They were copied while available, not rerun
or represented as full logs. Subsequent full logs include `service-green.log`,
`schema-red.log`, `schema-green.log`, `cache-red.log`, and
`cache-first-green.log`.

Expanded text stress initially failed: `text-first.log` reports 36 tests,
26 pass, 10 fail. Root cause was insufficient fixed caption capacity.
Wider slots/line budgets fixed accepted spaced-wide-word packing without
changing schemas or shrinking text. Later failures and corrections are
retained, including cache position RED (406 vs 238), moving-guide-caption RED,
a transient missing CacheColumn import during component extraction, and
outbound maximum-question/schema RED (12 tests, 11 pass, 1 fail). The final
outbound fix permits five question lines and four schema-label lines within a
186px card. `outbound-bound-green.log` is 12/12.

The literal-cell test initially overestimated combining-mark width by applying
a code-point advance helper directly to combining marks. It now measures base
advances and separately runs the reviewed SVG text-bounds oracle; production
raw strings were never normalized. Exact line concatenation, whole graphemes,
16 CJK characters, literal whitespace and empty cells are checked.

## Final verification

The final owned-suite command was the five test paths above passed together
to one `pnpm exec tsx --test` invocation, after the license guard.
`final-owned-tests.log`: **57 tests, 57 pass, 0 fail, exit 0**.
Tests include semantic identities, actual object/hand coordinates, paint order,
all target slots, exact category equality, local row boundaries, repeated row
occurrences, literal cell envelopes, backwards seeking, complete contracts,
translation extraction, 24 packing widths, 40 prefix lengths, and fixture
text bounds sampled every second frame.

```sh
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.tools.json
pnpm exec eslint src/stock/presets/{SharedJigPreparation,PortableWorkTransfer,ServiceablePanelSwap,SchemaPlanLocalExecution,QueryColumnCacheGrowth}
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/stock/presets/{SharedJigPreparation,PortableWorkTransfer,ServiceablePanelSwap,SchemaPlanLocalExecution,QueryColumnCacheGrowth}
git diff --cached --check
```

All exit 0. Source/tools TypeScript and ESLint logs are empty. Oxfmt reports
all 62 files formatted. The final static gates were rerun after the last
outbound-capacity correction. Initial ESLint duplicate imports and shadowed
fixture variables were corrected, with the original log retained.

From the repository root:

```sh
CI=1 pnpm exec react-doctor apps/ava-video-producer --yes --scope changed --base b08d3be504fa1a05026797bad514dba8beb79b55 --no-score --verbose
```

The first invocation skipped untracked files and is explicitly **not a clean
scan** (`react-doctor-skipped-untracked.log`). After staging only owned paths,
the one actual scan covered 62 files, exit 0, with eight warnings retained in
`react-doctor.log` and `react-doctor-diagnostics/`. This actual scan preceded the
final outbound card-capacity regression/fix. There was no score-service retry
and no repeat diagnostic run after that narrow correction.

- CacheCell positional key warning: reviewed as low impact, high confidence.
  Two stateless presentation lines use stable ordinal slots; no reorderable
  state or effects can attach to another cell.
- Seven array-lookup performance warnings: reviewed as low impact, high
  confidence. Validation/render lookups are over at most five columns and two
  requests. No unbounded workload or new shared optimization was introduced.

## Shared needs, limits and review concerns

No shared API changes are required. Controller-approved ruling 49 permits the
private CacheCell to split after eight whole grapheme clusters into at most
two fixed 12px LiteralDataText lines in a 168px column. Original raw value,
row index and column ID stay on the group; concatenated line values reproduce
the original exactly. Metadata records the literal whitespace convention.

SVG text assertions are conservative geometry estimates, not browser visual
approval or proof of all occlusion. The worker performed no Chromium renders,
frame gate, gallery build, full producer suite, or registry integration.
Controller serial default/dense/changed visual review remains required.
Some JSX-heavy drawing functions remain over the repository's 45-line target;
this is a known code-review concern rather than a claimed style pass.

## Changed paths

All 62 committed files are under these directories:

- `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/SharedJigPreparation/`
- `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/PortableWorkTransfer/`
- `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/ServiceablePanelSwap/`
- `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/SchemaPlanLocalExecution/`
- `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/QueryColumnCacheGrowth/`

The authoritative report and ignored evidence are task coordination artifacts.
The report is not part of the source commit. Downloads copies go to
`~/Downloads/avandar_motion-catalog/motion-atlas-packet-24/`.

| # | Owner | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Codex controller | Review immutable HEAD, then run serial visual QA and integration. |


## Correction1: Important findings 1-4

Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS. All four Important findings have scoped corrections
and regression coverage. Controller fresh review and visual QA remain required;
the review's Minor ledger is unchanged.

- Starting HEAD: `356caae65e88b14acab20b731086393e40d9b49b`.
- Correction HEAD: `ef93060a0aa0851dad832271ccf6d3a590e4bf76`.
- Commit: `fix(video): correct packet 24 handling and plan layout`.
- Scope: 15 files, 530 insertions, 196 deletions. The five owned directories
  plus Ruling 50's narrowly authorized localization test helper. Worktree clean
  after commit. No schema, fixture, default, contract, ID, or localization API
  changes. No registry/generated-file edits.

### Corrections and regression evidence

1. Accepted Portable copies now unload sequentially from the arrived folio
   onto its left-side destination surface. Each 240 by 80 copy ends at
   x=350..590, separated from the retained folio at x=640..904. Originals stay
   at x=50. The owner hand follows each moving copy's top edge during unloading;
   pending state remains covered. Tests measure emitted body bounds against
   the folio and bench, rigid copy dimensions, hand/arm contact, cover width
   and paint order across all fixtures.
2. The question/schema card crosses during frames 13..43, then settles into
   the remote lower region through frame 55. The returned plan uses the
   reserved y=108..198 lane during frames 56..100 and stays there. Retained
   headers move to baseline 312; 30px rows spaced every 32px keep all six rows
   within the same device. Remote exchange captions appear with their message
   phases in separate fixed 14px slots. Tests inspect every actual header
   tspan throughout return/hold, complete card text, both card envelopes,
   captions and retained row rectangles. Twenty accepted word-packing variants
   supplement default/minimum/dense/changed inputs.
3. `JigMarkingHand.tsx` separates the collaborator's arm, tool and hand from
   the underlying station. They paint after the single opaque guide. The
   corner hand fits inside the actual notch and the tool tip reaches its

# Motion Atlas Packet 24 review

**🟡 Needs fixes: 0 Critical, 4 Important, 4 Minor.**

## Spec compliance

**Issues found.** The five accepted schema/contract families are present, but accepted transfer unloading, returned-plan readability, and visible corner-guide handling need correction. **Task quality: Needs fixes.**

Reviewed immutable base `b08d3be504fa1a05026797bad514dba8beb79b55` through head `356caae65e88b14acab20b731086393e40d9b49b`: 62 added files and 5,514 lines. The supplied full-task diff was read once in seven bounded sections. Source references below are relative to `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/`.

## Strengths and verified requirements

| Preset | Source-backed assessment |
| --- | --- |
| SharedJigPreparation | One guide and collection-ordered applications retain all workpieces. Both patterns and material variants exist. `getJigSceneFromFrame.ts:13`, `JigPattern.tsx:29`, `SharedJigPreparation.test.ts:135`. |
| PortableWorkTransfer | Originals remain anchored, copies retain IDs, and pending state keeps an opaque cover with exterior labels. `PortableWorkTransfer.tsx:30`, `TransferArtifact.tsx:23`, `FolioCover.tsx:20`. |
| ServiceablePanelSwap | Target ID owns the slot, latch and connector. The removed original stays distinct, and unchanged neighbors retain coordinates. `getServiceSceneFromFrame.ts:8`, `ServiceablePanelSwap.tsx:19`, `ServiceablePanelSwap.test.ts:41`. |
| SchemaPlanLocalExecution | Only supplied schema/question enter the outbound group. Exact category equality determines local membership and the sum; hiding rows preserves the calculation. `PlannerExchange.tsx:27`, `LocalQueryResult.tsx:7`, `SchemaPlanLocalExecution.test.ts:139`. |
| QueryColumnCacheGrowth | One cache appends missing source columns without moving existing columns or changing row occurrences. `getCacheSceneFromFrame.ts:8`, `CachedRelation.tsx:21`, `QueryColumnCacheGrowth.test.ts:200`. |

All five co-named schemas use strict required objects, preserve accepted limits, and enforce their uniqueness/reference conditions. The schema files' exported `jsonSchema` and `semanticRules` retain the structural/semantic distinction. Their contracts contain versions, collection, 180-frame loops, binding examples and indexed default prose paths. The first three reuse `createStockControls`; the final two explicitly cover unsupported numeric and primitive-collection shapes. No content module imports a renderer. Supplied strings are not classified by English meaning.

Ruling 49 is implemented narrowly: `QueryColumnCacheGrowth/CacheCell.tsx:9` segments whole graphemes, splits after eight, preserves raw cell/column/row identity, and delegates exact text to `LiteralDataText`. The schema still accepts empty strings and the original <=16-character bound. The test at `QueryColumnCacheGrowth.test.ts:142` checks emitted raw-line attributes, concatenation, 12px text, CJK, joined/combining graphemes, whitespace and empty values. Cache rows use stable occurrence indices, so repeated B values remain separate.

## Critical

None found.

## Important

1. **Accepted copies never visibly unload from the folio.** `PortableWorkTransfer/getTransferSceneFromFrame.ts:23` moves packed copies from x=652 to x=660 with unchanged y. `TransferFolio.tsx:19` retains the folio at x=640, width=264; the 240px copies remain wholly inside it. Opening the cover therefore reveals a packed folio rather than placing copies onto the destination surface as required. Give accepted placement a visibly separate destination layout and test each copy's final geometry against the folio envelope. `PortableWorkTransfer.test.ts:55` currently proves only the success marker, not unloading.

2. **The returning plan obscures the retained table headers.** `SchemaPlanLocalExecution/PlannerExchange.tsx:55` moves an opaque 280x90 card from y=370 to y=184. It is painted after the headers at y=286 in `LocalRows.tsx:13` because of `SchemaPlanLocalExecution.tsx:18`. The controller's dense frame 90 shows the card covering both retained header labels. Reserve a collision-free return path and resting region, and assert card bounds against the complete header text envelopes during transit. Canvas-only text bounds do not detect this occlusion.

3. **Corner-mark mode paints over its marking hand.** `SharedJigPreparation/JigStation.tsx:73` fixes the hand at station x+20, y=382, equivalent to guide-local (70,32). The corner cutout is only guide-local (0..22,0..22) in `JigPattern.tsx:28`. `SharedJigPreparation.tsx:63` paints that opaque guide after the station, covering the hand and lower arm in the corner variant. Place the marking tool/contact at the selected pattern and paint the visible hand above the guide while preserving the guide's identity. The test at `SharedJigPreparation.test.ts:147` checks a hidden data marker, so it misses this failure.

4. **The same localization assertion logic is duplicated five times.** The 26-line test at `SharedJigPreparation/SharedJigPreparation.test.ts:108` is copied into `PortableWorkTransfer/PortableWorkTransfer.test.ts:126`, `ServiceablePanelSwap/ServiceablePanelSwap.test.ts:124`, `SchemaPlanLocalExecution/SchemaPlanLocalExecution.test.ts:112`, and `QueryColumnCacheGrowth/QueryColumnCacheGrowth.test.ts:112`. Extraction, synthetic translations, path traversal and immutability checks would all need synchronized fixes. The binding task-review rubric explicitly classifies verbatim logic-block duplication as Important. Request one narrow shared assertion helper through the controller, retaining preset-specific expected prose paths in each suite. No shared source edit was made during this review.

## Minor

1. **Several new JSX functions exceed the 45-line convention.** Examples: `SharedJigPreparation/JigStation.tsx:15` (69 lines), `SharedJigPreparation/SharedJigPreparation.tsx:11` (63), `SchemaPlanLocalExecution/LocalRows.tsx:8` (66), `SchemaPlanLocalExecution/PlannerExchange.tsx:8` (61), and `PortableWorkTransfer/TransferArtifact.tsx:13` (55). These already have recognizable responsibilities and no file exceeds 400 lines, so this is a bounded maintainability concern rather than evidence of behavioral failure. Extract meaningful drawing units such as a row, exchange card or artifact symbol.

2. **Exclusive child components sit beside their owners.** `PortableWorkTransfer/TransferFolio.tsx:2` owns `FolioCopies` and `FolioCover`; `QueryColumnCacheGrowth/CacheRequests.tsx:1` owns its cards/routes/missing-column children; `CachedRelation.tsx:2` owns `CacheColumn`, which owns `CacheCell`. The module-hierarchy convention places exclusively coupled descendants in the owning component's directory. Nest these private units without changing the required co-named public preset modules.

3. **Eight Doctor warnings remain in retained output.** Exact sites: `QueryColumnCacheGrowth/CacheCell.tsx:34`; `CachedRelation.tsx:50`; `QueryColumnCacheGrowth.schema.ts:55`, `:79`, `:91`; `getCacheSceneFromFrame.ts:9`, `:12`, `:14`. The positional keys represent two stateless, fixed line slots, and lookup collections are bounded at five columns/two requests. I agree these are low-impact diagnostics, not an important bug or performance defect. Retain their documented disposition; do not describe the scan as warning-free. Its final outbound-card correction was not rescanned.

4. **The maker's cutting arm dominates the figure.** `SharedJigPreparation/JigMakingTool.tsx:20` draws the elbow through (40,315) from the small maker at (80,440), then back to the cutting tool. The supplied default frame 36 shows an oversized angular shape competing with the guide. Shorten/reposition the articulated route while maintaining actual tool contact. This is visual clarity polish, separate from Important 3.

## Verification and limits

The worker reports 57/57 tests, both TypeScript checks, scoped ESLint, formatting and staged diff checks passing after the final capacity correction. These gates were not repeated. The retained Doctor log independently confirms one actual 62-file scan with eight warnings; the earlier untracked-file invocation is not evidence of a clean scan.

Focused checks outside the diff addressed named uncertainties only: the two shared assertion helpers were read to establish whether their advertised contract/text checks detect the identified failures. They validate top-level control coverage, valid bindings, deterministic seeks, text presence and estimated canvas bounds; they do not prove recursive editor behavior or object occlusion. The controller's existing dense planner frame 90 and default jig frame 36 were inspected read-only. No browser session, producer render, test rerun, source edit, or Git mutation was performed.

**Cannot verify from this task diff:** aggregate 150-addition counts and collection totals; preservation of the earlier subsets; registry wiring and complete omitted-input default resolution; integrated Lingui extraction/resolution and recursive editor behavior; the outer 960x600/30fps/1280x800 envelope, configurable background, seams and unchanged frame thresholds; final serial preview/browser/MP4 acceptance. These remain controller-owned. The diff contains only the five owned preset directories and does not alter the license guard, product source, adapters, generated catalogs or deployment/database state.

## Next Actions

| 1 | Codex controller | Return Important 1-3 to the worker with geometry regressions; coordinate the shared test helper for Important 4. |
| 2 | Codex worker | Correct findings within the authorized ownership boundary and report focused validation. |

# Motion Atlas Packet 25 review

**Specification compliance: Issues found. Task quality: Needs fixes.**

Counts: 0 Critical, 3 Important, 4 Minor. The three Important findings concern visible state and required transformation choreography. The accepted input domains and final calculations are implemented correctly in the reviewed source.

Base: `ef93060a0aa0851dad832271ccf6d3a590e4bf76`.
Head: `05cd7cd1daa472432fbcd832fe27820da0d9006d`.
Scope: the supplied immutable full-task diff, 188,697 bytes, 44 newly added owned files. Read once in eight contiguous bounded sections. No source or Git mutation, browser/composition rendering, subagents, or repeated test gates.

All source references below are relative to `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/`.

## Specification compliance

The five named renderers, strict inferred schemas, defaults, fixtures, metadata, explicit controls, structural JSON Schemas, semantic rules and typed renderer-free contracts are present. No unrelated production path appears in the diff. Important findings I1-I3 prevent specification acceptance.

| Requirement | Source evidence and assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical resource order and exclusive turns | `OrderedLockAcquisition/LockOperation.tsx:27` derives positions from the resource array; `getLockStateFromFrame.ts:14` separates acquire/release windows. Tests at `OrderedLockAcquisition.test.ts:36` and `:101` assert actual key coordinates and full card clearance. |
| Closed-before-mutation and complete replacement | `InvalidTableQuarantine/InvalidTableQuarantine.tsx:15` replaces the full row collection at frame 112, before opening begins at 113; `:23` completes closure at 45, before mutation at 46. Tests at `InvalidTableQuarantine.test.ts:45` and `:125` assert row values and shutter height. Caption inconsistency is I1. |
| Fixed entity grain, zero and null | `EntitySpineAssembly/EntitySpineAssembly.tsx:44` renders the entity array once; `EntitySpineRow.tsx:21` sums matching observations and preserves missing as null. Dense and zero assertions are at `EntitySpineAssembly.test.ts:27` and `:153`. Aggregation choreography is I2. |
| Seven picker rules and null policies | `GroupedValuePicker/getPickedValueFromInput.ts:3` preserves first-null, skips null for numeric rules, orders numeric mode ties before null and retains the unrounded mean. `GroupedValuePicker.tsx:17` rounds only mean display and selects countUnit. Tests at `GroupedValuePicker.test.ts:27`, `:52` and `:163` exercise exact values. Transform choreography is I3. |
| Stable identities and human work | `StatePreservingSourceRefresh/RefreshRecord.tsx:21` matches by exact ID and preserves status/assignee. `StatePreservingSourceRefresh.tsx:14` counts changed labels and absent records. Tests at `StatePreservingSourceRefresh.test.ts:126` assert every pinned region and actual text. |

Every schema uses strict nested objects and required fields, with the catalog collection and string/numeric bounds. Exact membership and uniqueness are enforced. In particular, `EntitySpineAssembly.schema.ts:18` retains the upper-only 12-character observation-ID bound, `InvalidTableQuarantine.schema.ts:9` and `:14` preserve empty replacement/reload strings, and `StatePreservingSourceRefresh.schema.ts:56` excludes new source IDs. No trimming, prose classifier or narrower accepted domain was introduced.

## Strengths

- Each contract explicitly lists default prose paths and is tested against a separately authored expected list. Examples: `EntitySpineAssembly/EntitySpineAssembly.contract.ts:25` with its test at `:107`, and `StatePreservingSourceRefresh/StatePreservingSourceRefresh.contract.ts:28` with its test at `:101`. Content modules do not import any renderer module.
- Unsupported control shapes have explicit numeric, nullable and primitive-item editors. The supported branches reuse the shared converter, including exact root-scoped references. Examples: `GroupedValuePicker/GroupedValuePicker.controls.ts:27`, `EntitySpineAssembly/EntitySpineAssembly.controls.ts:32`, and `OrderedLockAcquisition/OrderedLockAcquisition.controls.ts:80`.
- Regression checks go beyond diagnostic attributes in useful places: lock rectangle clearance, literal quarantine rows, the four-row concentrated entity spine, picker selection borders, and pinned human-region geometry. Limitations of those checks are recorded below.

## Important findings

### I1. Quarantine reports readable and blocked simultaneously

**Evidence:** `InvalidTableQuarantine/InvalidTableQuarantine.tsx:78`, with read state at `:26` and the side caption at `:70`.

Frames 13 through 45 are unreadable and display the blocked caption, but the upper caption remains `labels.readable` until frame 46. The default therefore says “Readable” and “Read blocked” together while the shutter closes. This contradicts the scene's central validity claim and the caption-ownership clarification. The controller independently observed the conflict in its frame-36 static preview.

**Fix:** Derive both validity captions from the same read state. Add assertions for the visible captions at closure start, intermediate closure, fully closed, and reopening boundaries. The current expected-text helper at `InvalidTableQuarantine.test.ts:84` repeats the defective frame threshold and must change with the behavior.

### I2. Entity aggregation does not visibly stack and collapse numeric contributions

**Evidence:** `EntitySpineAssembly/SpineObservation.tsx:24`, `:46` and `:49`; drawing order at `EntitySpineAssembly.tsx:32` and `:44`; opaque receiving bodies at `EntitySpineRow.tsx:35`.

Source cards and their numeric labels remain at fixed rail positions throughout frames 49-105. Only four-pixel dots move toward the receiving rows. Those dots are painted before the opaque spine bodies, so they disappear behind the bodies once their trajectory enters the row rectangle. In the seven-observation concentration, some dots briefly cross gaps between unrelated spine rows. At frame 106 the precomputed sum begins appearing independently. This does not implement the specified stacking of repeated observations beside their key and collapse of their numeric values by sum.

The unchanged shared palette confirms `STOCK.surface` is opaque. The controller's default/dense 70/90/105 static observations independently corroborate the absent visible aggregation.

**Fix:** Give numeric contribution groups an explicit per-entity stacking/collapse transition, with a deliberate foreground layer or unobscured destination. Preserve the source identities and fixed output grain. Assert actual intermediate contribution geometry and visible numeric aggregation for defaults and all seven observations on one entity, not just the final sum.

### I3. Picker calculation reveals a finished diagram instead of stacking or folding values

**Evidence:** `GroupedValuePicker/PickerCalculation.tsx:26`, `:29`, `:57` and `:73`.

For most-frequent, all frequency groups and tokens are created at fixed final coordinates and only the common opacity changes. For numeric rules, a fixed L-shaped path is drawn while the already-complete formula fades in. No observation value moves into a stack or onto the calculation line. The rail's only value-specific transition is the first-rule border in `PickerObservation.tsx:17`. The required first/stack/fold distinction is therefore only partially implemented; the metadata at `GroupedValuePicker.metadata.ts:132` promises a transformation the source does not perform.

**Fix:** Animate value-bearing copies from their rail positions into equal-value stacks or a numeric calculation line, retaining the source rail. Cover intermediate positions and grouping under count, mean, tied mode and included null. Existing hold-frame token-count assertions at `GroupedValuePicker.test.ts:158` do not establish this choreography.

## Minor findings

### M1. Two newly added fixture modules exceed the source-size limit

**Evidence:** `EntitySpineAssembly/EntitySpineAssembly.fixtures.ts:257` through line 513, and `StatePreservingSourceRefresh/StatePreservingSourceRefresh.fixtures.ts:254` through line 458.

The files repeat complete default records in every rejected case. The review rules require a split above 400 lines and always flag files above 500. Reduce repeated fixture setup while preserving complete runtime inputs, or keep the required fixtures entry module and move cohesive rejection/accepted data into a directory module. This is maintainability work, not an input-domain defect.

### M2. Scene functions exceed the repository function-size convention

**Evidence:** `InvalidTableQuarantine/InvalidTableQuarantine.tsx:10` spans 106 lines; `GroupedValuePicker/PickerCalculation.tsx:7` spans 82; `GroupedValuePicker.tsx:14` spans 75; `StatePreservingSourceRefresh/RefreshRecord.tsx:14` spans 88; `OrderedLockAcquisition/LockOperation.tsx:14` spans 69; `OrderedLockAcquisition.tsx:11` spans 84. The other entity/refresh scene functions also exceed 45 lines.

The repository asks for functions of at most 45 lines. Split coherent presentation units, such as result cards, request tiles, source comparisons and shutter state, into the owning preset directory. Keep the mathematical transitions together where that improves readability.

### M3. Helper organization and union dispatch miss explicit review conventions

**Evidence:** `GroupedValuePicker/GroupedValuePicker.tsx:89` declares `_getSelectLabel` below its caller and takes two positional parameters. `GroupedValuePicker/getPickedValueFromInput.ts:7` uses a plain switch for the rule union. The five co-named tests also declare two-argument `_render` helpers at line 17.

Place private helpers above their callers, use a named options input for multiple parameters, and use the repository's exhaustive union-dispatch convention. These are local consistency issues; no incorrect current picker result was found.

### M4. Explicit control descriptors retain template and empty copy

**Evidence:** `InvalidTableQuarantine/InvalidTableQuarantine.controls.ts:80` and `:85` use `PLACE.attempt.outcome.*` IDs instead of the preset namespace. Primitive editors at `:32` and `:123`, and `OrderedLockAcquisition/OrderedLockAcquisition.controls.ts:84`, carry empty label messages.

Finish these public descriptors with stable preset-scoped IDs and useful localized item labels. The source review does not claim a proven browser-accessibility failure, but these incomplete descriptors make the exported editor contract harder to understand and maintain.

## Verification and limits

- The worker report retains 52 focused passing tests, source/tools TypeScript checks, scoped lint, formatter and diff checks after narrow fixes. Those gates were not rerun. Tests assert real SVG attributes and text in addition to diagnostic state, but do not establish occlusion or the missing transitions in I2-I3.
- One exact-base React Doctor scan covered 44 files and reported four performance warnings. The frozen diff visibly uses Sets in the three flagged schema checks and a hoisted segmenter in `GroupedValuePicker/PickerObservation.tsx:7`. The warnings remain historical verification noise. No clean follow-up Doctor result is claimed or required by this review.
- Focused outside-diff check for the named occlusion/text-layout uncertainty: read `stockPalette.ts`, `LabelSlots.tsx`, `LiteralDataText.tsx` and `motion.ts`. This confirmed opaque row fill, fixed literal font sizing and clamped frame interpolation. None was modified.
- Focused outside-diff check for indirect assertion coverage: read `stockPresetAssertions.ts`, `registerStockTextLayoutAssertions.ts` and `registerStockLocalizationAssertions.ts`. The helpers check parse rejection, root control coverage, deterministic markup, canvas text estimates and explicit default-copy translation. Root control checks do not themselves prove every nested editor, and canvas estimates do not prove pairwise occlusion.
- Cannot verify from this diff: final registry inclusion, exact global addition totals and preserved subsets, compiled catalog/message extraction, integrated input omission behavior, configurable background and opaque envelope delivery, 1280x800/30fps export, final source fingerprints, browser playback or serial MP4/frame-gate acceptance. These remain controller-owned gates, not failures inferred from their absence here.

## Assessment

**Task quality: Needs fixes.** Exact data semantics and renderer-free contract assembly are strong, but contradictory validity copy and missing value transformations prevent trusting the explanatory animation as specified.

# Packet 26 specification and quality review

**Spec compliance: Issues found. Task quality: Needs fixes.**

**Findings: 0 Critical, 4 Important, 2 Minor.**

Reviewed immutable task base `d0645ef36e8c90bed6c36975609df98ba70b656a` through head `469223fd607ee07177153d310216084c8d2c2cce`. The supplied full-task diff contains 69 added files and 4,701 added lines, confined to the five assigned preset directories. The diff was read once in ten consecutive, bounded sections. This is the fresh task-scoped gate, not final branch or export acceptance.

Paths below are relative to `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/` unless another root is stated.

## Specification compliance

The five named components, strict schemas, exact defaults, fixtures, metadata and typed renderer-free contracts are present. The accepted numeric, collection, reference and literal-string domains are implemented without invented minimum lengths or prose classifiers. Distinct permission, transaction, transfer and spatial behaviors exist. The task cannot yet be accepted because transaction and PDF motion collide with visible copy, and the transfer retry caption does not identify its actual checkpoint. The ruling-line emphasis also needs polish.

| Preset | Verified behavior and evidence | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EffectivePermissionGrants | `getEffectiveRoleFromInput.ts:5` computes the maximum qualifying role. `PermissionLadder.tsx:14` raises the result separately from the required-role notch. `EffectivePermissionGrants.test.ts:116` checks order independence and hidden exclusions. | Compliant within this task review. |
| AtomicOutboxCommit | `OutboxDurableState.tsx:8` uses one durable boundary for the local value and ticket. `AtomicOutboxCommit.test.ts:44` samples every integer frame for both-or-neither state. The latch collides with the record caption. | Important fix required. |
| ResumableByteTransfer | `getByteTransferFromFrame.ts:17` partitions prefix and resumed chunks. `ResumableByteTransfer.schema.ts:21` enforces chunk count, acknowledgment boundaries and a positive pending suffix. Tests cover all six dense boundaries and the one-byte tail at `ResumableByteTransfer.test.ts:102` and `:119`. The retry caption stays at the file start instead of identifying the checkpoint. | Important fix required. |
| PdfGridReconstruction | `PdfGridReconstruction.schema.ts:22` preserves rectangular coordinate occurrences. `ReconstructionGrid.tsx:19` retains duplicate and empty cell values. Source/result overprinting breaks the requested visible reconstruction. Ruling evidence remains visible but weakened. | Important fixes required. |
| PdfNearestLabelReview | `getAssociationFromInput.ts:4` preserves both Euclidean distances and authored review. `PdfNearestLabelReview.schema.ts:41` accepts ties and coincident candidate anchors while excluding coincidence with the figure. Tests at `PdfNearestLabelReview.test.ts:110` cover threshold equality, farther choice and unresolved ties. Accepted corner anchors expose row/caption and row/guide collisions. | Important fix required. |

### Strengths

- Upper-only literal domains remain exact: empty record values at `AtomicOutboxCommit.schema.ts:8`, empty cells at `PdfGridReconstruction.schema.ts:9`, and empty label IDs versus null review at `PdfNearestLabelReview.schema.ts:15` and `:23`.
- Choreography has real intermediate geometry: candidate/rank movement at `GrantCandidate.tsx:17`, latch travel at `OutboxCommitMarks.tsx:6`, chunk travel at `ByteChunk.tsx:17`, table translation at `ReconstructionGrid.tsx:13`, and extending spatial guides at `CandidateAnchorGuides.tsx:14`. This is more than state-marker replacement.
- Every contract uses `satisfies StockContract<Input>`, complete schema/default/fixture bindings, explicit default prose paths and localized metadata. Representative evidence is `AtomicOutboxCommit.contract.ts:12`, `PdfGridReconstruction.contract.ts:25` and `PdfNearestLabelReview.controls.ts:77`. The latter preserves a nullable dynamic reference instead of narrowing the accepted empty-ID domain.
- Shared controls are reused for supported structures; explicit numeric and nested primitive controls stay local at `ResumableByteTransfer.controls.ts:15` and `PdfGridReconstruction.controls.ts:29`. Content modules in the diff do not import renderer modules.
- Independent localization-path expectations are registered, for example at `AtomicOutboxCommit.test.ts:104` and `PdfNearestLabelReview.test.ts:99`. The report clearly distinguishes retained test evidence from unperformed browser/export acceptance.

## Important findings

### I1. Keep the moving commit latch clear of the record caption

**Location:** `AtomicOutboxCommit/OutboxCommitMarks.tsx:6`; related `AtomicOutboxCommit/AtomicOutboxCommit.tsx:18`.

The latch is held at y=100 until frame 56 and is painted after the caption anchored at y=105. Its opaque 4px stroke spans x=100 through x=860, directly across the caption glyphs. This affects the ordinary default input, not only a dense edge case. The controller supplied default and dense static evidence, and this reviewer independently inspected the default frame-36 PNG, which visibly strikes through “Fictional stock note.”

Reserve a separate caption/latch envelope or change the latch route so its entire stroke remains clear throughout closure. Keep the single shared latch and atomic state boundary. Add a focused assertion for the complete moving latch versus the caption envelope; the current test at `AtomicOutboxCommit.test.ts:58` checks only the latch's y progression and stamp count.

Evidence: `apps/ava-video-producer/out/motion/packet-26-early/469223fd6/AtomicOutboxCommit-default-36.png`.

### I2. Preserve source and result readability while the grid unfolds

**Location:** `PdfGridReconstruction/ReconstructionGrid.tsx:13`; related `PdfGridReconstruction/ReconstructionCell.tsx:36` and `PdfGridReconstruction/ReconstructionHeaders.tsx:21`.

At frame 106 a second, fully visible grid begins at the source origin. It then translates from x=52 to x=508 over the retained source. Both copies have transparent cells and headers, so their glyphs and borders double-print throughout the overlapping part of the journey. The controller observed the defect at frames 110 and 122. This reviewer independently inspected dense frame 110: repeated headers, literal values and whitespace marks visibly merge. The motion loses the source-coordinate identity the reconstruction is meant to explain.

Stage the reconstruction so the complete source and value-bearing moving result remain distinguishable, with a clear final adjacent grid. Preserve every literal occurrence and the source relationship; an opaque sheet that simply hides the source is not a complete fix. Add intermediate default/dense geometry and paint-order assertions that cover all headers and data cells. The test at `PdfGridReconstruction.test.ts:59` currently proves only the first result rectangle's x/width, which passes through this overprint.

Evidence: `apps/ava-video-producer/out/motion/packet-26-early/469223fd6/103-110-122/PdfGridReconstruction/PdfGridReconstruction-dense-110.png`.

### I3. Keep the extracted row clear of the retained source and ratio caption

**Location:** `PdfNearestLabelReview/ReviewedExtraction.tsx:11`; related `PdfNearestLabelReview/ExtractionRow.tsx:19`, `:30`, `:37` and `PdfNearestLabelReview/AssociationStatus.tsx:22`.

For the accepted corner fixture with figure (5,5), a twelve-character CJK token and full candidate labels, frame 108 paints the moving token at y=507 across the ratio caption. At frame 118, the retained source anchor and distance guide cross the chosen-label glyphs inside the traveling row. Both collisions are visible in the controller's existing samples, independently inspected here. The current test at `PdfNearestLabelReview.test.ts:53` checks default x progression, not the complete text envelope against those fixed objects.

Reserve a travel lane and source-link route that keep the complete row, source anchors, guides and ratio caption readable for the full accepted coordinate range. Preserve the original token and distance evidence. Add an accepted low-x/corner regression that checks the row's value and chosen-label bounds at intermediate frames against fixed text and guide geometry.

Evidence: `apps/ava-video-producer/out/motion/packet-26-variants/469223fd6/108-118-130/PdfNearestLabelReview/page-corner-anchors/`, files `PdfNearestLabelReview-page-corner-anchors-108.png` and `PdfNearestLabelReview-page-corner-anchors-118.png`.

### I4. Attach the retry caption to the acknowledged checkpoint

**Location:** `ResumableByteTransfer/ResumableByteTransfer.tsx:25`; related checkpoint calculation at `:18` and checkpoint path at `:30`.

The caption “Resume here” always sits at x=84, the file's byte-zero start, while the checkpoint correctly moves with `acknowledgedBytes / sizeBytes`. No connector ties that caption to the checkpoint. In the accepted final-partial fixture, the checkpoint is at byte 4 of 5 near the far right, but the caption still points the reader to the far-left start. With offsets hidden this is the only authored retry label. This fails the explicit caption-ownership contract and obscures the difference between resuming and restarting, which is the preset's main point.

Anchor or visibly connect the complete retry caption to the checkpoint without overflowing at either edge. Cover zero, middle and near-end checkpoints with offsets shown and hidden. The marker assertion at `ResumableByteTransfer.test.ts:31` confirms the stored offset, but cannot establish which visible object the caption identifies.

Evidence: `apps/ava-video-producer/out/motion/packet-26-variants/469223fd6/36-90-150/ResumableByteTransfer-final-partial-chunk-150.png`.

## Minor findings

### M1. Retain and resolve the scoped Doctor key warning

**Location:** `PdfGridReconstruction/GridLiteralCell.tsx:36`.

The final scoped Doctor run reports `react-doctor/no-array-index-as-key` for literal line components keyed by array index. The current children are stateless and frame output is deterministic, so no visible state corruption is demonstrated and this is not an Important issue. It remains diagnostic noise in the reported final gate. Use stable occurrence identity if practical, or record an explicit narrow accepted exception rather than calling the output warning-free. Do not key by raw value alone because repeated and empty lines are accepted.

### M2. Strengthen the ruling-evidence reveal above the source grid

**Location:** `PdfGridReconstruction/PdfGridReconstruction.tsx:29`; related `PdfGridReconstruction/RuledGridEvidence.tsx:18`, `PdfGridReconstruction/ReconstructionCell.tsx:29` and `PdfGridReconstruction/ReconstructionHeaders.tsx:16`.

The actual early sheet shows the full grid at frame 13 and faint lighter line growth at frame 28. The evidence is not completely invisible, so this is a Minor visual-emphasis issue, not a missing transformation. Keep the selected evidence visibly distinct above or separate from the registered table outlines. The marker-only test at `PdfGridReconstruction.test.ts:46` cannot assess this emphasis.

Evidence: `apps/ava-video-producer/out/motion/packet-26-early/469223fd6/13-28-50/PdfGridReconstruction/PdfGridReconstruction-sheet.png`.

- Retained evidence reports 58/58 focused tests, both TypeScript checks, scoped ESLint/oxfmt and diff checks passing, with the single Doctor warning above. No reported gate was rerun.
- Named supporting risk: caption/literal coordinates and wrapping. Read only `LabelSlots.tsx`, `FitText.tsx` and `LiteralDataText.tsx`; confirmed SVG baselines and literal preservation.

These remain controller-owned. The diff leaves registries, shared envelope, licensing, original demos, footage and adapters unchanged.

The four Important findings prevent the visible transaction, spatial reconstruction/review and retry annotation from meeting the task's readability and caption-ownership requirements; marker, coordinate and canvas-bound checks do not close those gaps.

Three Important choreography findings and three Minor review groups. No Critical findings. The accepted input domains and final-state semantics are implemented, but three required transfers obscure the values they are meant to explain.

## Review scope

- BASE: `eb1f98ae613a1bc1c83e7968b062dba902fe0407`.

| Check | Evidence |

| Complete renderer-free contracts, recursive controls and literal public metadata | Each named `.contract.ts:16` assembles its schema, metadata, controls, defaults, fixtures and bindings using `satisfies StockContract<Input>`. Content modules do not import renderers. Region `.contract.ts:23` preserves tuple cardinality. |
