- Worktree: `/Users/juanpablosarmiento/src/worktrees/avandar/feat/motion-catalog`.
- Implementation is confined to `apps/ava-video-producer/`. The two helper
  modules and semantic type location follow the controller's R58 scope ruling.
- Git working tree is clean. No push, merge, PR, publication, database work,
  render, browser run, gallery build or English-message regeneration occurred.

## Implemented contract

`pnpm motion:catalog` calls the license guard, dynamically loads the
renderer-free registry, validates every complete default, fixture and binding,
checks every recursive control context, and then writes ignored output.
`out/motion/catalog` is an atomic directory symlink to a completed sibling
`.stock-catalog-*` generation containing both catalog files. A rejected input
leaves the previous generation intact. Existing ordinary directories at the
catalog path are rejected without deletion. Publication requires local
filesystem symlink and rename support.

The exported registry contains **170 records: 106 general and 64 social-sector**,
with **758 fixtures, 170 binding examples and 2,795 recursive controls**.
Membership is independently checked against the literal legacy20 IDs and the
accepted150 planning inventory. Runtime export does not import that planning
inventory.

The explicit record allowlist is: `id`, `schemaVersion`, `metadataVersion`,
`collection`, `loopFrames`, `metadata`, `jsonSchema`, `semanticRules`,
`defaultInput`, `defaultTextPaths`, optional `defaultSpanBindings`, optional
`displayCopy`, `controls`, `bindingExamples`, `fixtures`, `searchText`,
`searchTextHash`, and `contentHash`. Nested metadata, copy descriptors, control
variants, semantic-rule wrappers, and example wrappers are projected explicitly.
Complete authored inputs and structural schemas retain their own fields.
Runtime validators, source locators/hashes, source paths, proposal provenance,
`sourceRefs`, `proposalSources`, `mergedFrom`, and coordinator decisions are
excluded. The regression adds planning-only locators and hashes and requires
identical JSON, JSONL and public hashes.

The six R51 default span bindings and the optional R53 descriptor maps on all
20 legacy contracts are included as data. Source descriptors retain IDs and
messages. Complete defaults, fixtures, and supplied bindings are preserved
without translation or marker decoding. The literal marker regression keeps
`<content>Lieu</content> ` and UTF-16 offsets 9 and 13 unchanged.

`StockSearchMetadata` lives beside `buildStockSearchText` and contains only
semantic string fields. The exporter explicitly projects descriptor messages.
Search order is name, description, intent, creativeDirection, goodFor,
domains, aliases, tags, notFor, distinction. Whitespace is normalized within
each entry; empty entries are removed; authored array order is retained.
Defaults, fixture labels/counts, display copy, and binding prose do not enter
search text.

`searchTextHash` is SHA-256 of UTF-8 search text. `contentHash` covers the
canonical complete public record, including search text and excluding both
hash fields. Canonical JSON recursively sorts object keys, retains array order,
and excludes absent optional fields. There are no timestamps or source hashes.
Tests independently hash the emitted payload, change semantic description,
and change fixture labels/counts to verify the intended hash separation.

## R55 structural fidelity

The renderer-free `createStockJsonSchema` helper retains installed Zod's
`z.toJSONSchema`, targets draft-2020-12, and keeps unrepresentable constructs
in throwing mode. Its tuple callback supplies the minimum based on required
positional items, allows optional tails, caps fixed tuples at their positional
length, closes fixed tails with `items: false`, and preserves typed rest schemas.
Heterogeneous positional types and all runtime schemas remain unchanged.
Cross-field references, conservation, denominators, and prose obligations are
exported through the existing separately authored semantic rules.

Nine Zod assembly files use the converter: seven contract roots,
GeometryDetailBudget's coordinate item schema, and the legacy factory. The
legacy factory's two tuple-bearing contracts are NetworkGraph and NodeTraversal;
its non-tuple conversions retain their existing structural shape. Six missing
manual coordinate cardinality pairs were added across three editor files:
CatchmentUnionGaps, PopulationNormalizedMap and StratifiedSpatialSample.
No other manual schema fields changed. DocumentRegionDriftCheck's correct
explicit override and LocationUncertaintyBoundary's correct manual item schemas
are preserved byte-for-byte from BASE.

The focused scan covers all 170 contract schemas and recursive editor schemas.
It finds the ten tuple-bearing presets and verifies fixed cardinalities at every
prefixItems position. Behavioral witnesses cover missing/extra coordinates,
dimension tuples, heterogeneous positions, optional tails, optional-before-
required positions, typed rest, empty tuples and nested nullable arrays.
An independent test-only evaluator checks the JSON Schema keywords used by
these witnesses; it is deliberately not a general JSON Schema validator.
Control traversal handles nullable branches, empty primitive/variant paths,
numeric tuple positions, collections, unions and distinct root/item choice keys.
Unsupported referenced/intersected control contexts fail explicitly.

output in `task-6-evidence/<label>.json` and `.log`.

The converter now omits `prefixItems` when the positional item list is empty
(`createStockJsonSchema.ts:18`). Fixed-empty tuples retain `minItems: 0`,
`maxItems: 0` and `items: false`. Empty-prefix rest tuples retain their numeric
`items` schema without an artificial maximum. This removes the invalid empty
keyword while preserving the accepted JSON values.

## Evidence checked

The new assertions at `createStockJsonSchema.test.ts:129` and `:137` check
keyword omission and the respective bounds/rest schema directly. The typed
public fixture API at `:99` is `z.tuple([]).rest(z.number())`. Its independent

# Task 6 review: retrieval export

## Spec Compliance

**Issues found.** The actual 170-record export satisfies the reviewed retrieval requirements. One supported converter edge emits an invalid draft-2020-12 schema: empty tuples. R55 requires faithful structural export, so correct that representation before accepting the shared helper.

- BASE: `042a6c0e174870829d9360c1e247be66b6f86faa`.
- HEAD: `d8dfe9bb2e46f0c1535dd72437890dbac2594de7`.
- Reviewed the complete 1,966-line conventional diff package once, against the task brief including R55/R58 and binding review brief. All 22 changed files are under `apps/ava-video-producer/`. The source-hash manifest names these exact commits.
- **Quality: Needs fixes. Counts: 0 Critical, 1 Important, 2 Minor.** No implementation or Git state was changed during review. The only executed source check was a focused read-only tuple/override probe. Passing suites were not rerun.
- **Cross-task acceptance remains open.** Canonical generation, broad producer checks, gallery/browser acceptance, source freeze, previews, serial renders and frame gates remain with the controller. This review does not establish visual quality, timing, delivery dimensions or final runtime integration acceptance.

Paths below are relative to `apps/ava-video-producer/`, except evidence paths, which are relative to this review's SDD directory.

## Strengths and verified requirements

| Requirement | Finding and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Actual registry and membership | `scripts/export-stock-catalog.ts:63` dynamically imports the real registry after the guard. `scripts/stock/exportStockCatalog.test.ts:25` compares all IDs with literal legacy20 plus accepted150. Saved final tests pass. `task-6-evidence/repeatability.json` records 170 records, split 106 general and 64 social-sector. |
| Explicit public allowlist | `scripts/stock/createStockCatalog.ts:42`, `:104`, `:206` and `:233` explicitly project metadata, controls, localization data, rules and example wrappers. Authored input and structural schemas retain their fields. Source provenance and runtime validators are excluded. The provenance regression checks emitted JSON, JSONL and both hashes indirectly through byte equality. |
| Semantic text and hashes | `src/stock/search/buildStockSearchText.ts:16` preserves the prescribed field and array order, normalizes whitespace and omits empty entries. The string-only type contains no fixtures or provenance. `scripts/stock/createStockCatalog.ts:147` sorts object keys, retains array order and rejects non-JSON primitive values. `:261` hashes the complete public content before adding either hash field. The independent emitted-payload hash assertion is at `scripts/stock/exportStockCatalog.test.ts:373`. |
| Exact authored inputs and localization | `scripts/stock/createStockCatalog.ts:171` validates every default, fixture and binding and rejects transformed parse results. `:206` retains R51 spans and R53 display descriptors as data. The marker regression preserves authored text and UTF-16 offsets. No translator, marker decoder or renderer is imported. |
| Recursive control contexts | `scripts/stock/validateStockControls.ts:91`, `:105` and `:138` validate root/item choice paths, collection runtime and editor contexts, empty variant paths, numeric positions and nullable branches. References/intersections fail explicitly. The accepted nullable/union/dynamic-choice regression and false editor-field regression passed in the saved final run. |
| Tuple scope and fidelity | `src/stock/contracts/createStockJsonSchema/createStockJsonSchema.ts:8` retains installed Zod conversion, throwing mode and draft-2020-12. Nine conversion sites and six manual coordinate nodes are the narrow R55 correction. No runtime input schema, defaults or animation source changes. Fixed heterogeneous, nested, optional and typed-rest witnesses pass, subject to I1 below. |
| Existing explicit overrides | The preserved-file manifest keeps DocumentRegion's override and Location's manual schemas unchanged. A focused probe additionally confirmed that the schema regenerated for DocumentRegion by this exporter is deeply equal to its existing override. |
| Atomic publication and guard | `scripts/export-stock-catalog.ts:20` writes both files into a complete sibling generation before one symlink rename publishes it. Prepublication errors clean up the new generation, and validation occurs before any publication work. Existing ordinary directories fail at `readlink` without deletion. `:51` and `:63` guard direct API and CLI paths. No skip flag or telemetry call was added. The missing-license test has the narrower limitation M1. |
| Renderer-free closure | `task-6-evidence/final-renderer-free-closure.log` and `source-closure.json` record 963 local sources, zero forbidden imports, and only Node built-ins plus Zod externally. No planning inventory is imported by the production exporter; its test uses the accepted inventory as an independent membership oracle. |

## Issues

### Critical

None.

### Important

#### I1. Empty tuples produce an invalid JSON Schema rather than a faithful structural representation.

- Location: `src/stock/contracts/createStockJsonSchema/createStockJsonSchema.ts:23`; supporting test: `src/stock/contracts/createStockJsonSchema/createStockJsonSchema.test.ts:96`.
- The converter preserves Zod's `prefixItems: []` for `z.tuple([])`. Its cardinality override produces `{ type: "array", prefixItems: [], minItems: 0, maxItems: 0, items: false }`. Installed Zod accepts `[]`, but the emitted schema is itself invalid: draft-2020-12 requires `prefixItems` to be a nonempty array. See the [primary specification, section 10.3.1.1](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/draft-bhutton-json-schema-01#section-10.3.1.1).
- The test passes because its limited evaluator checks instances without validating schema validity. A conforming consumer can reject the schema before evaluating any instance. The same representation issue applies to a tuple with an empty positional prefix and a rest schema.
- **Scope and severity:** this is a shared-helper correctness defect in a shape the new tests explicitly claim to support. The saved 170-record catalog has **zero empty `prefixItems` nodes** across contract schemas and recursive controls, so this finding does not invalidate its current records or hashes. It is Important because faithful supported-shape export is an explicit R55 acceptance condition, not because the current catalog is broken.
- Fix: omit `prefixItems` when the positional list is empty, preserving fixed-empty bounds or the typed rest schema as appropriate. Add focused schema-validity regressions for empty fixed and empty-prefix rest tuples, alongside runtime acceptance witnesses. No runtime input narrowing is needed.

The focused probe exercised these exact operations against installed source:

```ts
const empty = z.tuple([]);
empty.safeParse([]).success; // true
createStockJsonSchema(empty); // Includes prefixItems: []
```

### Minor

#### M1. The missing-license regression does not observe the CLI's actual output location.

- Location: `scripts/stock/exportStockCatalog.test.ts:367`; CLI destination: `scripts/export-stock-catalog.ts:67`.
- The test asserts that the temporary directory used for the absent key file remains empty. The CLI writes to the fixed producer `out/motion/catalog` path, so an implementation that wrote output there and then threw the expected license error would still pass this assertion. The current guard ordering is correct by inspection; the coverage claim is broader than this test proves.
- Fix: isolate or observe the actual publication destination and assert that its prior state is unchanged after a missing-license invocation. Keep this nonblocking coverage improvement separate from the verified current guard behavior.

#### M2. The new catalog test file crosses the repository's 400-line split threshold.

- Location: `scripts/stock/exportStockCatalog.test.ts:179` and `:405`.
- This new 405-line suite mixes a large recursive-control fixture with filesystem/CLI publication cases and semantic/hash cases. The control fixture occupies most of the test beginning at line 179 and is a clear extraction seam. This is a minor maintainability issue, not a behavioral failure.
- Attempt a bounded extraction of reusable test setup while preserving the brief's prescribed public test entry. Do not reorganize production code to address this finding.

## Evidence reviewed

| Saved evidence | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `task-6-evidence/tuple-behavior-red.log` | 9 behavioral failures against the original conversion, including missing/extra tuple members. |
| `task-6-evidence/tuple-green.log` | 10/10 pass after converter adoption. |
| `task-6-evidence/export-red.log` | 9 expected failures against empty search/export implementations. |
| `task-6-evidence/publication-red.log` | Publication and direct-license assertions fail against no-op implementation. |
| `task-6-evidence/final-focused-tests.log` | 26/26 pass, no warnings, skipped tests or unresolved failures. |
| `task-6-evidence/final-helper-tuples.log` | 12/12 pass after the final evaluator extraction. |
| `task-6-evidence/final-helper-source-types.log` and `final-helper-tools-types.log` | Both compiler projects exit 0 with empty output. |
| `task-6-evidence/final-corrected-eslint.log` and `final-helper-eslint.log` | Scoped lint exits 0 with empty output. |
| `task-6-evidence/final-source-format.log` and `final-helper-format.log` | 21 source/config files and the final helper test pass formatting. |
| `task-6-evidence/command-index.json` | Exact argv, working directory, exit code and output are retained, including corrected intermediate failures. |
| `task-6-evidence/final-export-first-hashes.json` and `final-export-second-hashes.json` | Both export generations have identical byte counts and SHA-256 values. |

The two final exported artifacts also match the saved manifests on read-only inspection:

- JSON: 2,951,080 bytes; SHA-256 `96a818cc63424489e7bcc0216c33117bb5d270a7f04220af24716d56340ef0db`.
- JSONL: 2,951,048 bytes; SHA-256 `b74d6ec383d196264ae358cd6fd310ec3db25ccc747de1211a74009d3378312e`.

The source-closure manifest records compact-files-array SHA-256 `9829c784816b6b762d1cc58a1c66059ecc37a09753d70737d30d2ed457cde32f`. It is exporter evidence, not a final render freeze.

## Focused checks and boundaries

- **Named risk: optional/rest tuple domains could differ from installed Zod.** Read only installed `zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:2666` and `json-schema-processors.ts:373`. The converter's last-required-position calculation matches installed `getTupleOptStart`, and typed rest remains Zod's schema. Existing saved behavioral evidence covers the specified witnesses; those tests were not rerun.
- **Named risk: schema regeneration could discard DocumentRegion's explicit override.** Read its unchanged contract and ran a single focused `tsx` probe. `isDeepStrictEqual(createStockJsonSchema(contract.inputSchema), contract.jsonSchema)` returned `true`.
- **Named risk: recursive item/root scopes could disagree with the shared contract.** Read only `src/stock/contracts/StockContract.ts`; the exported projection retains every defined control variant and the shared localization fields. The saved regression exercises distinct root/item key names.
- **Named risk: an empty tuple could pass instance-only tests while being an invalid schema.** The same focused probe returned runtime acceptance of `[]` and the invalid empty `prefixItems` shape. The primary specification confirmed the constraint. A narrow read of the existing generated schemas/controls found no affected catalog record and confirmed the output hashes above. No exporter, renderer or suite was rerun.
- No source hunks required reopening a changed file. No browser, rendering, build, React Doctor, database, production, Git mutation or subagent work was performed. The PDF review is document QA only.

## Assessment

**Task quality: Needs fixes.** The exporter is well separated, deterministic and appropriately guarded, with useful behavioral RED/GREEN evidence. Correct I1's invalid empty-tuple representation before accepting the shared converter; the current 170-record export remains valid with respect to that finding.

This review was saved before artifact QA. Its synchronized Markdown/PDF location is `~/Downloads/avandar_motion-catalog/motion-atlas-retrieval-export/`.

source freeze, final export, browser acceptance, or media acceptance.

- Base: `550eff3673df2a5edfef71647cef015fbe5c76e9`.

  SDD. SDD means `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-motion-atlas-expansion/`.

## Strengths and requirement checks

1. **Exact registration and type boundaries.** The explicit contract registry

   86 and 64 additions respectively. The main map retains all 20 legacy entries
   (`src/stock/registry/stockRenderers.tsx:38`). The generic factory validates the
   selected preset before supplying `StockInputByPreset[Id]` to the component
   (`src/stock/registry/stockRenderers/createStockRenderer.ts:11`). No renderer
   import was added to the content registry. Independent membership and 106/64
   collection assertions are at `tests/stock.test.ts:95`. The saved final registry
   regression has three passing assertions, including deterministic SVG and
   sibling-local definitions.

2. **Bounded discovery preserves the guarded entry point.** Enumeration traverses
   only `src`, `scripts`, and `tests/helpers`, plus direct `tests` and `showcase`
   files. It rejects hidden, dependency, output, generated directories and does
   not follow symbolic links. Missing directories are tolerated; other filesystem
   errors propagate (`scripts/testing/enumerateProducerTests/enumerateProducerTests.ts:4`,
   `:36`). The runner retains the license guard, forwards Node test options and
   propagates unsuccessful child exit status (`scripts/testing/runProducerTests.ts:5`).
   The fixture tests both inclusion and exclusion, including colocated helper
   tests and excluded E2E tests (`enumerateProducerTests.test.ts:8` in that directory).

3. **All sixteen upper-only paths are corrected without changing other rules.**
   The precise unified hunks remove only `.min(1)` from PairedContrast's three
   paths, CapabilityMatrix's three, DecisionFork's four, TradeoffPivot's shared
   gain/concession ID, and the four remaining preset ID fields. Upper bounds and
   refinement bodies are unchanged. Manual and schema-derived control metadata
   agree, including `CapabilityMatrix.controls.ts:28` and `:61`. The eight
   schema/render cases include valid empty IDs, duplicate-empty rejection and
   finite markup (`src/stock/presets/upperOnlyBounds.test.ts:25`). ScopeAperture
   now puts arbitrary IDs in a fixed attribute value (`ScopeAperture/ScopeTopic.tsx:36`),
   with an explicit space/Unicode regression at `upperOnlyBounds.test.ts:171`.
   A focused unchanged-renderer check found strict equality for empty focused or
   selected IDs in PairedContrast, CapabilityFocus and DecisionFork.

4. **DOM identity and validation are corrected at their real boundaries.**
   SelectField locates values by strict equality and maps option indexes to
   private DOM tokens; empty authored strings and numeric/string twins no longer
   collide. Unknown values select only the disabled placeholder and remain in
   draft state (`src/gallery/MotionGallery/ContentControls/SelectField.tsx:26`).
   Actual DOM regressions assert selected option text and state after changes
   (`tests/editor-controls.test.ts:422`, `:444`, `:472`). The E2E selectors now use
   authored visible labels (`tests/e2e/motion-content.spec.ts:115`, `:159`), but
   that browser spec has not been executed in this phase.

5. **The two confirmed text/validation defects have genuine behavioral evidence.**
   ForkLabel segments tokens with a hoisted grapheme segmenter, retaining the
   existing width calculation and append behavior
   (`src/stock/presets/DecisionFork/ForkLabel/ForkLabel.tsx:4`, `:34`). The combining
   mark and seven-wide-glyph joined-emoji cases each fail independently against
   BASE and pass after the correction (`ForkLabel.test.ts:132`). WordReveal skips
   the unavailable fourth mask while its original max-length schema still rejects
   four words ordinarily (`src/stock/presets/WordReveal/WordReveal.schema.ts:23`,
   `WordReveal.test.ts:5`). Neither fix changes accepted text maxima or timings.

   stationary and detour-endpoint contact with the blocked open interior, while

   rounding and Arial/Courier advances. Optional node details and empty metric
   units are preserved. The shared contract replaces vague fit prose with these

8. **PF-01 and PF-02 describe current behavior.** SavedSeedSeasonReturn now explains

10. **R51 and R54 remain distinct and bounded.** The added ledger witness checks
    omitted translated default text and exact UTF-16 offsets at the StockGraphic

  not executed exports. L3's real HTTP/native-download acceptance and the separate

`accepted-29-30-contract-audit.json`, `configured-export-coverage-26-30.json`, and
`task-7-source-evidence/current-renderer-closures.json`. The final pair hashes

`22226ad7d1e98f12e52d992a678335a451a41e7148589d73c69f4c15f21ac12f`.
Matching hashes reuse static inspection only.

## Issues

### Critical

None in the source-integration scope.

### Important

None in the source-integration scope.

### Minor

**M1. A disclosed Doctor warning remains on the option key.**
`src/gallery/MotionGallery/ContentControls/SelectField.tsx:43` still uses
`${option.value}-${index}` as the React key. The index-based key existed before
this patch, but the requested scan continues to flag it. Reordering reference
options therefore changes element identity unnecessarily. A type-qualified value
key, with explicit duplicate handling if needed, would remove the warning without
changing the private DOM value tokens. This is a carried warning, not evidence of
an incorrect selected value: the controlled selection and real-DOM tests cover
that behavior. Evidence: SDD `task-7-source-evidence/react-doctor.log:19`.

The other Doctor warning, constructing Intl inside the wrapper, is resolved by

## Cannot verify here: later gates

  Task 6 must correct fixed tuple cardinality in both public `jsonSchema` and

  The final accepted matrix identifies GeometryDetailBudget's coordinate tuple

  default and configured MP4s, unchanged frame gates, actual L3 HTTP download and
  final documentation remain pending. Source tests cannot establish those gates.

## Validation and review method

The retained command JSON and logs establish separate behavioral RED failures and
successful focused GREEN runs. I inspected the actual saved failures for DOM
identity, combining/emoji segmentation, WordReveal's TypeError, empty bounds,
missing discovery, semantic omissions, translated sinks and the snapshot stroke.

Final relevant saved results include 24 restored localization checks, three

immediately before the final segmenter hoist. Scoped formatting and lint passed,
including post-hoist checks. The single Doctor command used the exact BASE and
`--scope changed --no-score`; its remaining warning is M1. No tests, Doctor scan,
browser, animation render, producer build, or Git command were rerun by this reviewer.

The full supplied diff was read once in bounded chunks. Truncated tool-output
segments were recovered. The controller supplied a conventional unified diff to
resolve colorless difftastic hunks that concealed token deletions; only ambiguous
schema hunks were read from that supplement. No changed source file was separately
reread. Focused unchanged-source checks addressed three concrete risks:

   `CapabilityMatrix/CapabilityFocus.tsx:10`.

No production source, index, HEAD, branch state, credentials, external service or
product component was mutated. Only the requested review artifacts were authored.

## Assessment

**Specification verdict: Compliant for this source phase.**
**Quality verdict: Approved with one carried Minor.** The narrow fixes preserve
runtime domains and renderer/content separation, and the focused evidence exercises
observable failures. Final Task 7 acceptance remains explicitly incomplete.

# Task 7: Gallery authored whitespace correction

**Status: bounded editor correction complete, with native line-ending limitations.**

## Scope and ownership

- Worktree: `/Users/juanpablosarmiento/src/worktrees/avandar/feat/motion-catalog`
- Base: `02d6cfbb66577931dd7d7eb19f9c06ef5b1a431a`
- Commit: `498c717d5` (`fix(motion): preserve authored gallery text whitespace`)
- Sole production writer: Codex task agent `atlas_editor_whitespace`. No subagents were used.
- Coordinating agent owns showcase PID 53692 on port 4183. Its lifecycle was untouched.
- Chromium was exclusively held for focused headless E2E, then this report. No concurrent browser, render, or PDF work was started.
- No actual HTTP export, MP4 rendering, frame gating, or global media acceptance was performed by this task. The coordinator owns fresh review and configured N1 acceptance.

## Root cause and correction

Ordinary text descriptors selected `input type=text`, although their schemas accept LF. Real field filling followed by native clipboard copy reproduced the N1 mismatch: `A\nB\tC\nD\nE` became `A B\tC D E`. The explicit multiline branch already used a textarea.

Every generic text descriptor now uses a native textarea. Ordinary controls start at one row with wrapping off and can be resized vertically. Explicit multiline descriptors retain their prior default row count and soft wrapping. Native labels, field IDs, descriptions, validation flags, and maxLength remain attached to the visible control. No hidden JSON authoring path or application whitespace transformation was added. Textareas receive the existing invalid-border styling.

Number and boolean controls still use native inputs with the same conversion, bounds, step, and checked behavior. Select, union, nullable, collection, draft validation, descriptors, schemas, defaults, and renderers were not changed.

## Files committed

| File under `apps/ava-video-producer/` | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/gallery/MotionGallery/ContentControls/ScalarField.tsx` | Use native textareas for all text controls, preserve descriptor sizing, and narrow the remaining input helper to non-text scalars. |
| `src/gallery/MotionGallery/ContentControls/ContentControls.module.css` | Retain invalid styling on textareas and allow vertical resizing. |
| `tests/e2e/motion-content.spec.ts` | Add native clipboard whitespace/export-input regression and native CR/CRLF paste/copy coverage. Keep the existing branch editor regression. |

No source files outside the authorized editor/test scope were changed. This ignored SDD report and its Downloads copies are the required reporting artifacts.

## Red/green evidence

All browser commands ran from `apps/ava-video-producer`, against the existing server. The producer config uses headless Chromium, one worker, zero retries, and a 45-second local timeout. Each test was run separately.

Exact red command:

```sh
REMOTION_KEYS_FILE=/Users/juanpablosarmiento/src/avandar/apps/ava-video-producer/.env.local pnpm exec playwright test --config playwright.motion.config.ts tests/e2e/motion-content.spec.ts --grep 'authored whitespace' --workers=1
```

Before production changes: exit 1, one failed test in 719 ms. The failure was the exact native copied-JSON mismatch described above, at the `copied.input.approach` equality assertion.

Exact final green command for the same regression:

```sh
REMOTION_KEYS_FILE=/Users/juanpablosarmiento/src/avandar/apps/ava-video-producer/.env.local pnpm exec playwright test --config playwright.motion.config.ts tests/e2e/motion-content.spec.ts --grep 'authored whitespace' --workers=1
```

After correction: exit 0, one passed test in 741 ms, 2.0 seconds total. Visible top-level and collection text fields preserve submitted LF, TAB, leading/repeated/trailing literal spaces, decomposed `e` plus U+0301, and joined emoji sequences in native copied configured JSON. Schema parsing returns the same object. Live SVG labels retain the exact approach and priority content. The Download MP4 button submits the same input, schemaVersion, accent, and background as copied JSON.

The export endpoint is deliberately intercepted with HTTP 400 in this regression after capturing the outgoing request. This proves UI transport payload equality only. It does not create, download, inspect, or approve a real rendered MP4. The existing branch test separately checks its already-mocked download transport.

Exact CR/CRLF green command:

```sh
REMOTION_KEYS_FILE=/Users/juanpablosarmiento/src/avandar/apps/ava-video-producer/.env.local pnpm exec playwright test --config playwright.motion.config.ts tests/e2e/motion-content.spec.ts --grep 'native pasted CR' --workers=1
```

Result: exit 0, one passed test in 564 ms, 1.8 seconds total. Native clipboard paste of `A\rB\r\nC\nD\tE` produces `A\nB\nC\nD\tE` in the visible control and native copied JSON.

Exact existing-flow green command:

```sh
REMOTION_KEYS_FILE=/Users/juanpablosarmiento/src/avandar/apps/ava-video-producer/.env.local pnpm exec playwright test --config playwright.motion.config.ts tests/e2e/motion-content.spec.ts --grep 'edited branches' --workers=1
```

Result: exit 0, one passed test in 767 ms, 2.1 seconds total. Collection editing/removal, invalid selection feedback, disabled actions, preview retention, corrected selection, copied request, mocked download content/payload, reset, and dialog focus return still pass.

Intermediate observations were resolved before the final green: an anchored title filter matched no tests; an initial immediate run still served the prior gallery bundle; an SVG label selector matched both a parent group and text node. The filter was corrected, the licensed gallery builder completed, and the preview assertion was scoped to its first authored label. No production change was made in response to these test-harness issues. Browser runs print the inherited NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR warning.

## Native CR/CRLF limitations

The [HTML textarea standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-textarea-element) defines its API value with LF line endings. This task observed actual Chromium clipboard paste converting CR and CRLF to LF. Accordingly, these controls preserve authored LF/TAB/Unicode/spaces, but cannot promise arbitrary-byte or original CR-versus-CRLF round trips through native editing. No application normalizer was introduced to conceal this limitation.

A separate investigation using Playwright `fill` with CR produced a different automation result: Chromium retained literal CR characters in that insertion path. The first assumption that this automation path would match native paste failed. The committed regression therefore exercises actual clipboard paste and checks the resulting native control and copied JSON, rather than treating automation insertion as evidence of universal CR preservation or normalization.

Textarea Enter inserts LF. TAB can be pasted and is preserved. Keyboard Tab retains native focus navigation. The compact one-row control can scroll or be resized to edit additional lines. Exact preserved editor content does not promise that glyph layout paints literal whitespace: existing stock text layout intentionally normalizes display whitespace, and was not changed.
